Weight loss drugs have been linked to hair loss, a new study has claimed.

People on GLP-1 agonist drugs, such as Mounjaro, Ozempic and Wegovy, have been reporting hair loss to regulators and a new study on around 50,000 people appears to support the link.

GLP-1s are primarily used to treat diabetes and obesity by mimicking hormones to regulate blood sugar and reduce appetite.

Experts used data to compare rates of alopecia hair loss in adults using GLP-1s to manage diabetes with those on other drugs.

The team from the University of Pennsylvania Health System noted that regulators in the US have been informed of the link between the drugs and hair loss, particularly for semaglutide (Wegovy and Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro).

So far in 2026, the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has received 399 reports of hair loss relating to tirzepatide, alongside 541 last year.

It has also received 148 reports of hair loss linked to semaglutide, alongside 164 reports last year.

For the new study, the team looked at people with type 2 diabetes on GLP-1 receptor agonists or other types of diabetes drugs known as SGLT-2 inhibitors, or DPP-4 inhibitors.

open image in gallery A person using pre-filled injection pen of Mounjaro ( PA )

In total, 12,004 patients using GLP-1s were compared with 15,221 using SGLT-2 inhibitors and a further 11,964 GLP-1 users were compared with 11,233 DPP-4 inhibitor users.

After adjusting for factors that could influence the results, such as age and weight, researchers found using GLP-1 drugs were associated with a 37% higher risk of alopecia than use of SGLT-2 inhibitors.

GLP-1s were also linked to a 68% higher risk of hair loss than use of DPP-4 inhibitors.

Further analysis suggested the link related to non-scarring alopecia (where hair follicles remain intact, leaving the potential for hair to regrow).

The researchers, including from the University of Pennsylvania in the US, wrote in the British Medical Journal (BMJ): “Case reports and analyses of the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)’s Adverse Event Reporting System have described occurrences of hair loss following initiation of a GLP-1 receptor agonist, particularly semaglutide (Wegovy and Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro).

“In response, the FDA has indicated that it is evaluating this potential safety signal.

“Although hair loss does not typically result in physical harm, it may have significant psychosocial consequences, affecting self-esteem, quality of life, and adherence to treatment.”

On the reasons why people may suffer hair loss while on the drugs, the team said the “most likely mechanism” relates to weight loss and “reduced caloric intake”, though more research is needed.

They said restricting calories may “contribute to physiological stress and micronutrient deficiencies (for example, iron, zinc, biotin), which can disrupt the hair growth cycle”.

open image in gallery Weight-loss drug Wegovy ( PA )

Other factors may include the “metabolic, hormonal, and immunological effects attributed to GLP-1 receptor agonists that may influence hair follicle growth and cycling”.

For example, GLP-1 receptor agonists have been associated with changes in thyroid function, and delayed gastric emptying may alter the absorption of orally administered drugs, including thyroid hormone or sex hormone therapies, they said.

“Such changes could influence hair growth through endocrine mechanisms, particularly in individuals with underlying hormonal conditions.”

The team concluded: “Our findings extend previous anecdotal safety signals and provide more systematic evidence to inform clinical awareness of this potential adverse effect.”

On Wednesday it was revealed the drugs have also been linked to a fall in the number of people who are dependent on alcohol being admitted to hospital.

Studies suggest the medication could help curb alcohol consumption.

However, researchers in the US said the evidence “remains limited and mixed”.

News.title: Inflation fall a ‘false dawn’, Burnham warned
News.content:
Falling inflation is a “false dawn” for Andy Burnham, economists warned after the pace of price rises slowed in June.

The consumer prices index (CPI) fell from 2.8pc in May to 2.6pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics (ONS), beating economists’ expectations of a drop to 2.7pc to mark the lowest rate in 15 months.

Lower petrol and diesel prices drove the slowdown amid a short-lived peace deal between the US and Iran, while price pressures from chocolate, oils and fats, dairy and meat also weakened.

However, economists warned a rise in household energy bills in July may already have pushed inflation back up above 3pc.

Suren Thiru, chief economist at the Institute of Chartered Accountants, said: “June’s slowdown is a false dawn as it may have already been reversed this month with higher energy bills, following Ofgem’s energy price cap rise, likely to have lifted inflation above 3pc.”

July’s 13pc increase in the energy price cap has pushed typical annual bills to around £1,862, while renewed fighting between the US and Iran has reignited concerns over oil and gas supplies.

Mr Thiru said elevated inflation would create a fresh headache for John Healey, the newly appointed Chancellor, by squeezing household budgets, raising government borrowing costs and limiting his room for tax cuts or spending increases.

Charlotte O’Leary, at the National Institute of Economic and Social Research, said: “June’s peace deal and the subsequent reduction in oil and gas prices helped cool consumer price inflation. This will be a welcome figure to start the new Prime Minister’s premiership, but the honeymoon period will be short-lived.”

The Bank of England will also be watching closely as it weighs further interest rate cuts, though economists warned renewed instability in the Middle East and higher energy bills could keep inflation close to 3pc for the rest of the year.

Mr Healey said: “Falling inflation is news families want to hear, but there is much more to do to give people the breathing space they need.”

News.title: Russia destroys Ukraine HIV warehouse
News.content:
A Russian missile strike has destroyed $2.6m (£1.9m) worth of HIV prevention supplies in Ukraine, according to an international aid group.

The Alliance for Public Health said the attack on Sunday night near Kyiv hit a warehouse holding 62 million prevention items earmarked for Ukraine’s harm reduction programmes next year. It includes syringes, needles, alcohol wipes, and condoms intended to support more than 300,000 people.

“This is not just another strike. It is an attack on 300,000 Ukrainians who depend on HIV prevention services and on their fundamental right to health,” said Andriy Klepikov, executive director of the Alliance for Public Health.

Efforts to prevent the spread of HIV rely heavily on harm reduction programmes that supply sterile syringes and needles to people who inject drugs, alongside condoms and other supplies that help curb sexual transmission.

Mr Klepikov said the destruction of the warehouse would not immediately disrupt services, because his organisation had moved its supplies for the rest of the year out of central storage and into regional distribution centres several weeks ago as part of contingency planning.

“Russia failed,” he said, adding that the Alliance had notified international partners and appealed for urgent support to rebuild next year’s inventory.

News.title: Private sector pay suffers worst growth since Covid
News.content:
Private sector wages are growing at their slowest pace since the pandemic, piling pressure on Andy Burnham as he enters Downing Street facing a fragile economy and strained public finances.

Salaries rose by 2.9pc in the three months to May, the first time growth has dipped below 3pc since October 2020 and only narrowly ahead of inflation at 2.8pc.

The slowdown was most acute in key industries, with wages in finance and business services up just 2.3pc, manufacturing at 2.5pc and construction earnings falling by 0.2pc over the year.

In contrast, public sector pay accelerated to 5.5pc after striking workers secured higher settlements, widening the gap between state and private sectors.

The cooling labour market came as borrowing overshot official forecasts, leaving John Healey, the new Chancellor, with a £2.7bn gap against expectations.

The Government borrowed £57.6bn between April and June – less than a year earlier but still ahead of projections – pushing public debt to nearly £3tn, or 94.9pc of GDP.

Mr Healey said: “The Prime Minister and I have talked about how we will work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty and how we’ll make life more affordable for working people right across the UK.”

However, Sir Mel Stride, the shadow business secretary, said: “If Andy Burnham and John Healey are really serious about the future of our economy then they must get borrowing under control.”

News.title: Scammers stole $114 billion as Southeast Asia’s crime gangs go corporate
News.content:
Scam gangs stole up to $114 billion from people in Asia-Pacific alone in 2025, the UN has warned, as crime syndicates rapidly professionalise their tactics to evade law enforcement in Southeast Asia.

By way of comparison, the sum dwarfs the $85 billion the UK spends each year on defence.

The Asia-Pacific region has emerged as an epicentre for massive cyber fraud operations since the Covid pandemic. Scammers – some willingly, others under duress – are now stealing billions from internet users across the world via fake romance and cryptocurrency investment schemes.

In 2025, these fraud operations stole between $88.3 and $114.1bn from just people across East Asia, Southeast Asia, Australia and New Zealand, according to a report on Tuesday from the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).

Those figures are triple the estimated losses in 2023, between $18 and $37bn, and don’t account for victims in Europe or the US.

The scam centres – which began in fortified compounds but are now increasingly housed in innocuous office blocks and villas – are found across the region, but have especially exploited power vacuums caused by war, corruption and weak governance in Cambodia, Myanmar and Laos.

Although the scammers initially targeted people in China, they have dramatically expanded their ambitions. The UNODC said people from at least 80 countries and territories had been identified in compounds, with recruiters seeking people from outside Asia as they look to expand new markets.

News.title: UK borrowing costs rise at fastest pace in G7
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs rose at the fastest pace in the G7 after Andy Burnham said he would take a “flexible” approach to the UK’s fiscal rules.

In his maiden speech as prime minister, Mr Burnham on Monday signalled he could bend the rules underpinning Britain’s finances, spooking financial markets fearful of higher government spending.

UK gilts – a benchmark for how much the Government pays on its debt – saw yields rise 0.08 percentage points to an eight-week high of 5.03pc for the 10-year bond. Thirty-year gilts also pushed higher.

The rise was the fastest in the G7, excluding Japan, whose markets are closed for a national holiday.

After markets closed on Monday, Mr Burnham surprised the City by picking John Healey as his next Chancellor.

Mr Healey, who quit over defence funding rising too slowly, will now be tasked with finding billions of pounds in Britain’s stretched public finances.

Shabana Mahmood, the Home Secretary, had widely been expected for the role. Ed Miliband, the former Energy Secretary, was also in contention.

Mr Healey will replace Rachel Reeves, who resigned on Monday.

The appointment of Mr Healey, a veteran of the Blair-Brown government, may calm fears in the City after Mr Burnham pledged to stretch the fiscal rules by using “flexibility” within them.

Speaking in Downing Street, Mr Burnham said: “I’ve said we’ll stick to the fiscal rules, and by that I mean the existing fiscal rules, and use obviously any flexibility within them.”

James Athey, a fund manager at Marlborough, said: “It’s not a good start because bandying around the words fiscal rules seems to be believed within government circles to be a sufficient condition to get financial markets on side, and that just misunderstands an element of the problem.”

He added that investors were watching closely for any signs that the Government will increase borrowing.

Matt Amis, investment director at Aberdeen, said Mr Burnham’s comments had “got the markets’ attention.”

He said “It just shows this week in particular the language from the Burnham administration, the new chancellor, is going to be key here. The gilt market is on edge.”

Mr Burnham, who has become the UK’s seventh prime minister in just a decade, has inherited a troubled economy as businesses grapple with low confidence and strained public finances.

Monday’s comment suggests the new prime minister will use measures to raise borrowing while keeping the additional sums off the Government’s book.

The Resolution Foundation, a think tank, said he could do this by expanding the remit of institutions like the National Wealth Fund, an arms-length government investment vehicle.

His plan to use “flexibility” in the fiscal rules comes after Ms Reeves altered the main indicator of government debt in 2024.

She tweaked the primary measure of the UK’s debt to Public Sector Net Financial Liabilities, meaning that when public financial institutions borrow to invest in a private business it does not count towards the government’s fiscal rules.

However, the think tank warned that boosting the financial capacity of public financial institutions like the National Wealth Fund by £16bn would cost around £400 million a year in debt interest.

Helen Miller, director at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, warned that challenging public finances will mean Mr Burnham will be forced to make tough choices on spending.

She said: “While chancellors come and go, the underlying fiscal constraints remain the same. Public debt, borrowing and debt-interest costs are all high. One in every £12 the government spends currently goes on debt interest.”

Higher borrowing costs threaten to increase the Government’s debt interest bill, which is already forecast to hit £111.2bn for the financial year - equivalent to 8.3pc of public spending.

Mr Burnham said he would announce a set of measures on Tuesday to give households “breathing space” to help with the cost of living.

“I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them,” he said.

“We will help more young people into education... and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down, to meet our fiscal rules and to honour our commitments on defence to our international partners.”

Mr Amis said: “Tomorrow we’re getting some cost of living news. [Burnham] said he was going to state where that funding’s come from. I think that’s key, any unfunded spending from here would get the market’s attention.”

News.title: India approves first dengue vaccine as cases surge in South Asia
News.content:
India has approved its first dengue vaccine as cases of the mosquito-borne disease surge in South Asia.

Japan’s Takeda Pharmaceutical’s dengue vaccine QDENGA has been approved by India’s drug regulator, the Centre Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO).

The global threat posed by dengue has been rising for years, as climate change, urbanisation and international travel aid the spread of the mosquitoes that transmit it.

The approval comes as hospitals across South Asia grapple with a surge in dengue infections.

In Sri Lanka, health authorities reported 2,652 new cases on Sunday alone, taking the total to 76,044 dengue cases so far this year. At least 53 people have died.

Bangladesh is also suffering a major outbreak with over 9,000 cases and 30 deaths that has piled pressure on its health system even as it battles a measles epidemic.

Dengue is transmitted to humans through the bites of infected Aedes mosquitoes.

Its symptoms include fever, severe muscle pain, and in severe cases, shock and internal bleeding that can be fatal.

Although mortality is relatively low, outbreaks place a substantial burden on health systems.

Takeda’s QDENGA jab is a live-attenuated tetravalent vaccine designed to protect against all four dengue virus serotypes. It can be given regardless of previous dengue infections.

“The approval comes at a critical time for public health, as reported dengue cases in India have increased 11-fold in the past two decades,” the company said in a statement.

News.title: Burnham’s plan to restore UK aid spending
News.content:
Andy Burnham is planning to reverse the cuts to Britain’s aid budget made by his predecessors Sir Keir Starmer and Rishi Sunak, according to reports.

A roadmap for returning the UK to spending 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on international aid will be drawn up as part of a major shake-up of the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), The Independent reported.

Ed Miliband is set to be named Foreign Secretary and put in charge of overhauling Britain’s international development aims, as well as prioritising climate goals, senior Labour sources said.

The aid spending plan was absent from Mr Burnham’s brief first speech as Prime Minister, in which he pledged to end rough sleeping and bring down the welfare bill in order to fund defence and council housing.

But it follows anger within the Labour Party over what was seen as a broken manifesto promise, when Sir Keir and Rachel Reeves, the Chancellor, slashed aid spending to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

Senior Labour MPs have been lobbying for a return to the 0.7 per cent commitment, a target first established by the United Nations in the 1970s.

It has since become a key yardstick for international efforts to reduce poverty and tackle major health issues like the HIV/AIDS epidemic, vaccine access, and maternal mortality in poor countries.

Sports.title: Wolves striker breaks silence after being BANNED from training ground as security called in
Sports.content:
Wolves striker breaks silence after being BANNED from training ground as security called in

Wolves striker Tolu Arokodare has spoken out after suggestions that he refused to leave the Championship side’s training ground following a disagreement with new boss Cesar Peixoto

View 2 Images Tolu Arokodare has spoken out on reports that he has been banned from Wolves' training ground (Image: Getty Images)

Wolves star Tolu Arokodare has hit out at reports that he refused to leave the club’s training ground, forcing their pre-season preparations to be cancelled. It was suggested that the Nigerian frontman refused to leave the pitch after being told to leave the playing surface.

‌



He had reportedly been asked not to train with the rest of the squad. Further security was then deployed the following day to ensure he was not able to enter.

‌



Arokodare, 25, has now spoken out and claimed that he didn’t actually do anything wrong but wanting to train.

‌



Taking to social media, he said: “I was very surprised and disappointed to see the media reports today, many of which are inaccurate. Throughout my career, I have always taken great pride in conducting myself professionally and maintaining the highest training standards.

Southampton boss Tonda Eckert charged by FA over Spygate saga and could face ban READ MORE :

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

"My commitment has always been to prepare myself as well as possible so that I can contribute to my team-mates and the club whenever I am called upon.

"I remain under contract with Wolves, and my only intention is to fulfil my responsibilities professionally by training, doing my job, and contributing to the team in accordance with that contract."

‌



Arokodare joined Wolves last summer in a £23.4m move from Belgian side Genk. But he struggled to adapt to the demands of Premier League football, with just three goals in 33 appearances, as the club slipped in the Championship.

Wolves took on Maidenhead in a pre-season friendly on Wednesday but Arokodare was not involved in any capacity. A number of clubs are already interested in signing him, with his future now up in the air.

View 2 Images Tolu Arokodare scored just three Premier League goals last season (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Fiorentina were initially interested but have now used up all of their assigned non-EU spots within their squad so have been forced to abandon a move. That has seen Serie A rivals Genoa express an interest in the forward, while Dutch giants Ajax are keeping tabs on developments.

Wolves have already bid farewell to a number of first-team stars ahead of their first season back in the Championship. Joao Gomes completed a £35m move to Aston Villa last week, while Matt Doherty has departed for second-tier rivals Sheffield United.

Wolves have also made a few signings, with Raul Jimenez and Ladislav Krejci rejoining the club, while Rafiki Said and Kieran Trippier have also penned deals with the Black Country side.

Sports.title: Jurgen Klopp set to appoint TWO ex-Liverpool coaches in Germany backroom team
Sports.content:
Jurgen Klopp set to appoint TWO ex-Liverpool coaches in Germany backroom team

Jurgen Klopp has taken his first job in international management having been appointed as Germany boss and he is now set to be reunited with two of his former Liverpool colleagues

View 2 Images Klopp is set to sign a four-year deal with the DFB (Image: Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp is due to be reunited with former Liverpool coaches after being appointed Germany boss. The 59-year-old is expected to be officially appointed as head coach of his country soon.

‌



Ahead of his unveiling, Klopp has been making decisions over the backroom team that he wants in situ at the DFB - and it appears that he is keen on a couple of reunions.

‌



According to Sky in Germany, both Pep Lijnders and Peter Krawietz are expected to be appointed to his team, the pair having worked closely with him during his time at Liverpool.

‌



Speaking about the pair’s relationship in 2020, the former said: “There’s a super dynamic between us. It’s much more than just assistant and manager. What I mean by that is that I believe you need 100 per cent trust in this job because we have to make so many decisions on a daily basis.

"I love working for him. He sees who I am, and respects that. We know what to expect from each other.

Liverpool confident of beating Arsenal to £100m star as they move on second winger READ MORE :

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

“Jurgen is a true leader. He’s inspirational and motivational. He still surprises me every day with something he says. His brain works differently to a lot of other brains!

‌



“He sees through situations and processes. There is a saying that people don’t care how much you know until they know how much you care.

"And I think everyone who works with Jurgen has the feeling he really cares about you and your development. There is no ego, he purely searches for the right thing to do.”

View 2 Images Klopp is set to be reunited with Pep Lijnders (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Since then, Lijnders has embarked on a managerial career of his own, having had a seven-month spell with Red Bull Salzburg. He then returned to the Premier League after being appointed as an assistant to Pep Guardiola at Manchester City - a job Klopp encouraged him to pursue.

“The moment Pep called, and the feeling he gave me about what he wanted to do with the team by bringing me in, the trust he already had before we discussed how it would look, that made the decision much easier,” Lijnders said.

“But you cannot put away 10 years of Liverpool that easily. But I’m really proud to come to a club of this magnitude, so successful over the last 10 years and with a manager that defined football. When I spoke with Jürgen he was so clear: ‘If you don’t do it, I will take the assistant job.’”

Article continues below

Elsewhere, Krawietz worked with Klopp at Liverpool until his departure in 2024. Sven Bender is also expected to be named as part of the new set-up within the German national side.

Sports.title: Five standout World Cup stars Liverpool could sign next to answer Andoni Iraola plea
Sports.content:
Five standout World Cup stars Liverpool could sign next to answer Andoni Iraola plea

Liverpool have only made two signings so far this summer but could look to World Cup standouts for their next recruits

View 6 Images Liverpool will have Andoni Iraola at the helm for the upcoming season (Image: Getty)

Liverpool have only made two summer signings so far with the new Premier League season under a month away. Mohamed Salah is also yet to be replaced, but one £100million World Cup star could be the answer.

‌



The Reds have thus far parted with a combined £100m for defender Jeremy Jacquet, whose transfer was sealed in January, and winger Victor Munoz.

‌



But Andoni Iraola's team is likely to need a few extra squad members if he's to inspire a Premier League title charge. The Spanish manager, who guided Bournemouth to European football for the first time in their history last term, has stressed the need to sign a winger and bolster their defensive cover.

‌



If the club wish to answer his plea, they could look at some players who stood out at the World Cup for potential recruits. Mirror Football has a look at five stars who shone in North America.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Andoni Iraola now has something Arne Slot and Jurgen Klopp never did at Liverpool READ MORE :

Ferran Torres

Every World Cup final requires a hero and this year's was Spain and Barcelona winger Ferran Torres. The 26-year-old hammered home the winner in New Jersey after the match had entered extra-time and this proved sufficient to clinch a 1-0 triumph.

‌



View 6 Images Torres won the World Cup for Spain (Image: Getty)

While an entire nation celebrates him, at club level, Torres' future remains unclear. Reports in Spain indicate Barcelona would move him on in the coming months.

With Liverpool seeking a winger, the former Manchester City player could suit their needs, although the rumours emerging from France this week that the Reds are poised to go toe-to-toe with PSG for his £40m signature are unfounded.

‌



Bradley Barcola

Finding a replacement for Salah is unquestionably Liverpool's primary objective and France forward Bradley Barcola remains linked with a switch to Anfield. The PSG winger shone for Les Bleus in the States, frequently displacing stars such as Desire Doue and Rayan Cherki from Didier Deschamps' starting XI.

He also found the net three times during the competition. It's understood that Barcola would command a fee exceeding £100million. Despite this, The Athletic has reported that Liverpool are keeping close tabs on his situation and would be keen to bring him into their squad.

View 6 Images Barcola could replace Salah (Image: Getty)

‌



Barcola has two years left on his deal and the general view is that he'll depart this summer. That said, the Reds would probably encounter competition from other European heavyweights should they chase the 23-year-old.

Ibrahim Mbaye

One of PSG's emerging stars could become Liverpool's present. Senegal heartbreakingly departed the World Cup, being forced to extra time by Belgium, only to be eliminated after new Manchester United signing Youri Tielemans slotted a 125th-minute penalty.

View 6 Images Mbaye starred for Senegal (Image: Getty)

‌



But Ibrahim Mbaye shone. He netted against France in the group stages and displayed brilliance out wide, featuring in his nation's 5-0 victory over Iraq.

At merely 18, the PSG winger isn't yet established, but neither is a player like Rio Ngumoha, who many would prefer to see handed a starting role by Iraola in the forthcoming season. Reds supporters are accustomed to witnessing Senegalese talent flourish at Anfield and L'Equipe claims that Mbaye could be secured for between £34m and £42m, which might prove to be genuine value.

Maxim De Cuyper

Shifting away from wingers, left-back might be another area of worry for Iraola this campaign, considering that Robertson has departed and Milos Kerkez appeared exposed at times last season under Arne Slot.

‌



View 6 Images De Cuyper could be a great addition to Liverpool's squad (Image: Getty)

Consequently, recruiting another left-sided full-back who won't cost the earth to share duties with Kerkez, should Kostas Tsimikas be deemed surplus to requirements in the forthcoming weeks, could be under consideration.

Belgium's Maxim De Cuyper was linked with a switch to Anfield before joining Brighton, and he impressed for his country at the World Cup, featuring from the start in five matches during their run to the last eight. He would represent good value and already has top-flight experience in England.

‌



Jarell Quansah

Liverpool will require defensive reinforcements with Konate's departure and Virgil van Dijk's slowing down. They may soon turn to one of their former academy prospects.

Admittedly, Jarell Quansah's World Cup was hardly flawless. His dismissal against Mexico in the last 16 was an impulsive tackle and nearly eliminated the Three Lions.

View 6 Images Quansah only left Anfield in 2025 (Image: Getty)

Article continues below

However, the 23-year-old England defender, who departed for Bayer Leverkusen last summer in a £35m deal, impressed against Panama and appeared remarkably assured at right-back versus France.

Quansah offers flexibility, understands what's required to represent the Reds and would return a considerably more experienced professional should his boyhood club bring him back. Though if Anfield officials hold off for a year, they will allegedly have a £56.2m buy-back option to trigger.

Sports.title: Arsenal dream squad for 2026/27 season after £80m lesson learned and six signings made
Sports.content:
Arsenal dream squad for 2026/27 season after £80m lesson learned and six signings made

Arsenal must act fast to secure key signings after missing out on several top targets

View 4 Images Arsenal are having a tough time in the transfer window (Image: Stuart MacFarlane, Arsenal FC via Getty Images)

With pre-season training already underway, Arsenal are entering a critical phase of the transfer window that will likely shape their upcoming campaign. After winning the 2025/26 Premier League title, the Gunners got their summer business off the ground by securing defender Piero Hincapie permanently for £34.5 million.

‌



They also managed to pull off a smart sale, sending 31-year-old Leandro Trossard to Besiktas for roughly £17m as he entered the final year of his contract. His successor has also been targeted, with the signing of Christos Tzolis set to be announced this week. A £34m sum was agreed for the Club Brugge winger, who registered an incredible 51 goal involvements last term.

‌



Still, several priority positions remain untouched. Arsenal are still short on a defender, central midfielder and a high-profile forward. The story of the summer has been rivals repeatedly beating them to key targets. Manchester City landed teenager Jeremy Monga, while Chelsea hijacked Arsenal for Morgan Rogers – paying Aston Villa's full £117m price tag after the Gunners backed off at an £80m valuation.

‌



With time ticking down toward the September 1 deadline, sporting director Andrea Berta and manager Mikel Arteta need to act fast. Here is a look at the essential moves the English champions must complete before the window closes if they want to give themselves the best shot at defending their title.

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Break the bank

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is worth over £100m in the current target (Image: Getty)

‌



The greatest obstacle to Arsenal's transfer business so far this summer has been their unwillingness to break the bank. While it is commendable that Berta refuses to pay over the odds for a player, he must acknowledge that the market is currently inflated and eye-watering fees are simply the price of doing business for elite talent - even if that means going £15-20m beyond an initial valuation.

Failing to do so while rivals such as Chelsea, Tottenham and City casually splash over £100m on a single player will only leave them short of the quality required once the season gets going. Julian Alvarez and Bradley Barcola are the two names consistently linked with a switch to the red half of north London, and both would command fees comfortably in excess of £100m.

To avoid a repeat of the Rogers situation, they must get the chequebook out. Barcola is a regular starter for France and fits the profile of player Arteta has been crying out for on the left flank — blistering pace and exceptional dribbling ability.

‌



The winger is open to leaving PSG in pursuit of a more prominent role elsewhere and would be an outstanding alternative to Rogers for the Gunners. Any further hesitation only heightens the risk that Liverpool or another rival snaps him up, or that PSG refuse to sanction his departure if they run out of time to bring in a replacement.

Alvarez's situation remains equally interesting. The World Cup finalist is eager to join Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid are firmly opposed to strengthening a direct La Liga rival.

While Atletico maintain that Alvarez is not available, they are reportedly more receptive to approaches from Arsenal, though it would take a potentially record-breaking Premier League fee to persuade them to part ways with him.

‌



Depending on the funds available and Atletico's final position, Berta must secure either Barcola or Alvarez within the coming weeks.

£80m Bruno Guimaraes transfer

View 4 Images Bruno Guimaraes should be an Arsenal player next season (Image: Getty )

Similar to the forward market, midfielders are commanding astronomical fees this summer. Earlier in the transfer window, the Gunners refused to splash the cash on Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali, both of whom joined rivals Tottenham.

‌



They have subsequently pinpointed Newcastle's Bruno Guimaraes as a main target, capable of either replacing or partnering Declan Rice, who has been managing an ongoing injury concern. The Brazilian midfielder is eager for a switch to north London, though the two clubs remain at odds over his price tag.

Arsenal have established a firm valuation for the player and will only advance with the transfer if Newcastle are prepared to negotiate within those boundaries. Considering the current market, £80m would represent a sensible maximum offer for Guimaraes.

Should Newcastle insist on an even higher sum, Berta should concentrate all of his efforts on securing Alex Scott, a younger alternative with considerable resale potential in the future unlike Guimaraes, from Bournemouth. Reports indicate Scott has recently rejected a new contract with the Cherries amid attention from several Premier League sides, including Arsenal, suggesting he would be obtainable if the Guimaraes deal fails to materialise.

‌



Land free agent

View 4 Images John Stones would be an excellent signing (Image: CameraSport via Getty Images)

The defence is also in need of immediate attention. At the start of the summer, Arsenal were understood to be in the hunt for a new right-back, given the persistent injury concerns surrounding Jurrien Timber and Ben White.

However, White has since returned to training while Timber is closing in on his own return. Instead, central defence has become a problem area for Arteta, with L’Equipe reporting William Saliba could be sidelined for as long as four to five months, with surgery potentially necessary to resolve his persistent back issue.

‌



Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa is reported to have emerged as a possible target. However, Villa are reluctant to let the England defender leave and have reportedly placed a substantial price tag of between £50m to £60m on him.

Such a sum is excessive for someone who would merely provide cover for Saliba once the Frenchman makes his return. Moreover, Cristian Mosquera has already demonstrated his capability in filling Saliba's shoes and Konsa would hinder the youngster's development.

A more astute alternative would be to sign John Stones, who departed Manchester City this summer, on a free transfer. There are undeniably question marks surrounding the World Cup star's fitness record and capacity to remain available over an extended spell.

‌



But Arsenal don't require a long-term replacement for Saliba, simply an experienced head who can rotate with Mosquera until their key man is back in contention. And, considering he previously worked with the player at City, Stones would represent Arteta's perfect solution.

Full squad list

Here is how Arsenal’s full squad list could look at the start of the 2026/27 Premier League season, with incomings and outgoings considered:

Goalkeepers: David Raya, Kepa Arrizabalaga, Illan Meslier.

‌



Defenders: Jurrien Timber, Ben White, William Saliba, John Stones, Cristian Mosquera, Marli Salmon, Gabriel Magalhaes, Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapie.

Midfielders: Declan Rice, Martin Zubimendi, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Bruno Guimaraes, Martin Odegaard, Eberechi Eze, Ethan Nwaneri.

Forwards: Bukayo Saka, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Viktor Gyokeres, Kai Havertz, Bradley Barcola, Christos Tzolis, Gabriel Martinelli.

Article continues below

Sold: Fabio Vieira, Reiss Nelson, Christian Norgaard, Gabriel Jesus, Leandro Trossard.

Signed: Piero Hincapie, Christos Tzolis, Illan Meslier, Bruno Guimaraes, John Stones, Bradley Barcola.

Sports.title: The World Cup hidden gems Arsenal, Man Utd and Premier League rivals should sign
Sports.content:
The English transfer market appears out of control with a premium on any player with a sniff of Premier League experience - £117m for Morgan Rogers, £116m for Elliot Anderson, £100m for Sandro Tonali and £85m for Mateus Fernandes.

So plenty of clubs will have been on the lookout for a bargain deal from the hundreds of players who were on show at this summer's World Cup.

Now, we'll freely admit signing players based on a strong World Cup doesn't always work out - see case studies Karel Poborsky, Kleberson, Marcos Rojo (all Manchester United).

That's why, when compiling a list of the best value players from every position at the tournament who could make a difference in the Premier League, we've also looked at their numbers at club level to reveal a clearer picture of what these players can do.

‌



Using Machine Football's model, we can uncover the World Cup's hidden gems and identify the clubs where they could make the biggest impact.

World Cup awards in full as Golden Boot, Player of the Tournament and Young Player decided READ MORE :

Goalkeeper: Raul Rangel, 26 (Guadalajara, Mexico; True Value: £10.2m)

View 15 Images Raul Rangel of Mexico (Image: Getty Images)

The goalkeeping ranks produced fewer stand-out bargains, but this shot-stopper's performances over the summer have elevated him into that category.

Rangel actually entered the World Cup off the back of a steady but unspectacular Liga MX campaign with Club Deportivo Guadalajara, starting all 32 matches and playing 2,880 minutes.

‌



He faced 116 shots across the season, saving 66.4% of them, while conceding 39 goals at 1.22 per 90. Guadalajara's third-place finish reflected a strong team campaign, but Rangel's individual numbers did not suggest a goalkeeper ready to make a major impact on the international stage.

The World Cup, however, told a very different story. Rangel started all five of Mexico's matches, playing 437 of a possible 450 minutes, and produced numbers far beyond his domestic baseline.

Per Machine Football's tournament tracking, he faced 2.01 shots on target per 90 and made 1.46 saves, conceding just 0.55 goals per 90. His expected-goals-saved figure of 0.85 across the tournament shows he prevented almost a goal more than he should have done, given the quality of chances faced.

Your World Cup glossary of football tactics, data and stats buzzwords READ MORE :

He was also composed in possession, completing 91% of his passes and 80% of his goal kicks, while coming off his line 0.91 times per 90 to deal with danger.

‌



Four of Mexico's five matches ended in clean sheets, an 80% rate that more than doubled his best full-season domestic return.

The numbers were backed up by moments of individual quality. Against South Korea, Rangel produced one of the saves of the group stage, using his foot to deny a close-range header before recovering instantly to claw away the rebound and preserve Mexico's second consecutive clean sheet.

That contrast is exactly what makes Rangel an intriguing profile. His club numbers have yet to reflect the level he reached on the international stage, suggesting a goalkeeper whose ceiling may be higher than his domestic record indicates.

Verdict: For clubs searching for a high-upside option, the World Cup offered evidence that there could be more to unlock. Hull City and Newcastle United are on the hunt for a keeper.

‌



Right-back: Alex Freeman, 21 (Villarreal, USA; True Value: £7.25m)

View 15 Images Alex Freeman of the USA (Image: Getty Images)

USA defender Alex Freeman's father, Antonio, won a Super Bowl with the Green Bay Packers. The younger Freeman, though, has forged his own path - breaking through with Orlando City before earning a January move to Villarreal, where he is yet to nail down a spot or register a domestic goal involvement.

The World Cup told a different story entirely. He started all five of the USA's matches, playing 100 minutes against Belgium, 110 against Bosnia-Herzegovina, 105 against Australia - where he scored - and 103 against Paraguay, where he assisted.

Across those 441 minutes he won 5.7 duels and completed 6.9 progressive passes per 90. A goal, an assist and elite ball-winning numbers from right-back all inside the same tournament – this was a genuine breakout for a 21-year-old still finding his feet at club level.

‌



Freeman's numbers from MLS last year suggest he won't have to wait too long to make that next step. From 27 starts at Orlando City in the regular season 2025, Freeman bagged six goals from right-back while laying on three assists for his teammates, also making more touches in the opposition box (132) than any other full-back in the division.

Verdict: So which Premier League side actually needs him? David Moyes's Everton ranked in the 36th percentile for offensive duels won and 29th for defensive duels last season, a side losing individual battles at both ends of the pitch. Freeman's all-round game, not simply his ability to overlap, looks like a direct answer to that problem.

Every Premier League summer transfer as Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool splash the cash READ MORE :

Right centre-back: Jhon Lucumi, 27 (Bologna, Colombia; True Value: £21.2m)

View 15 Images Colombia's Jhon Lucumi facing Portugal (Image: Alex Gottschalk/DeFodi Images/Shutterstock)

Classed as an 'Enforcing 4' by the Machine Football model, Lucumi is an old-school defender focused on winning duels rather than dictating games in possession.

‌



The World Cup provided the perfect test of that profile. Colombia started him in all five matches, including the full 127 minutes of their penalty-shootout defeat to Switzerland.

Across 538 minutes he completed 91.7% of his passes and won 1.7 aerial duels per 90 at a rate of 72.7%, combining composure with remarkable durability. With Lucumi at the heart of their defence, Colombia conceded one goal over the course of their five-game run to the round of 16, managing a four-game streak of clean sheets.

Lucumi was a regular starter in Serie A for Bologna last season and demonstrated a knack for sweeping up effectively, with his 5.23 recoveries per 90 higher than 95% of other centre-backs in the division.

Verdict: Where does that profile find a home? Xabi Alonso has only just arrived at Chelsea, but the Blues' lack of physical prowess was there for all to see last season, and it didn't improve as the managers changed.

‌



Under Enzo Maresca, the manager that oversaw most of the minutes, they ranked in the 27th percentile for aerial duels and 14th for defensive duels. Under Liam Rosenior, who took over next, both numbers got worse. Caretaker Calum McFarlane's brief spell saw aerial duels fall further still.

Three managers, one problem which none of them managed to improve. Lucumi's profile targets it directly.

Left centre-back: Facundo Medina, 26 (Marseille, Argentina; True Value: £19m)

View 15 Images Facundo Medina in the World Cup final (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Lionel Scaloni gave left-footed centre-back Facundo Medina just 162 minutes at the World Cup, starting him against Cape Verde before bringing him off the bench in the World Cup final.

Even so, Medina completed 86.4% of his passes, including in the biggest match of the tournament, and won 63.6% of his duels.

Such a low tournament sample size is an obvious caveat, and Medina also only started 16 games in Ligue 1 last season. Despite that, he possesses a quality on the ball that could make him a solid option as a centre-back-left-back hybrid for a Premier League side.

Creativity is a rare strength for a centre-back, yet Medina ranks in the 97th percentile globally — a genuinely elite reading regardless of position. A regular for Marseille, he also sits in the top 5% for passing accuracy and is classified as a Complete 4 in Machine Football's category of player styles.

‌



Verdict: That passing profile is exactly why Arsenal stand out as a potential destination. Despite their miserly defensive record at home and in Europe, Mikel Arteta's side's defensive duels stats were not great. However, that reflects dominance rather than a weakness.

Arsenal simply keep the ball so effectively that opponents have fewer opportunities to engage them in defensive battles.

Arsenal already have a squad built around that identity. William Saliba and Cristhian Mosquera are both classified as Complete 4s – the same archetype as Medina — so his appeal is not that he introduces something unfamiliar, but that he provides a more polished, ready-made version of a profile Arteta already trusts.

View 15 Images Facundo Medina's solidity, technical ability and tactical flexibility could make him a good fit for Arsenal or Crystal Palace (Image: Machine Football)

‌



Given Arsenal already have two left-footed defenders who can play both wide and centrally in Riccardo Calafiori and Piero Hincapie, though, a club like Nottingham Forest could also suit Medina - where he would be expected to feature on the left of Oliver Glasner's back three in a role similar to the one Marc Guehi played at Crystal Palace.

Left-back: Ghislain Konan, 30 (Gil Vicente, Ivory Coast; True Value: £1.5m)

View 15 Images Ivory Coast's defender Ghislain Kona (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Ghislain Konan started three of four Ivory Coast matches on their run to the round of 16, averaging 7.7 progressive passes and 2.4 crosses per 90.

That's genuine attacking output from a left-back in a side that reached the knockout rounds. Konan was also a regular starter for Gil Vicente in Portugal's top flight last season, and no full-back in the division made more dribbles (1.72) or recoveries (5.68) per 90.

‌



Konan combines experience with attacking intent, and would suit a side who like to bypass central areas and create down the flanks.

Verdict: Which side could that be? Frank Lampard's Coventry City are a no-nonsense sort of side that completed the second-most crosses per 90 last season while ranking just fourth for possession, despite storming to the Championship title with 95 points.

Konan could provide experience and quality for a side who will be mainly focused on survival.

Right defensive midfielder: Lamine Camara, 22 (Monaco, Senegal; True Value: £40m)

View 15 Images Senegal's Lamine Camara against Iraq (Image: AP Photo/Stephanie Scarbrough)

‌



The highest-profile player on this list so far, Machine Football ranks Camara in the top 5% globally for his attacking contribution value, rare creative numbers for a holding midfielder.

The 22-year-old started for Senegal against France, Norway and Iraq at the World Cup, registering an assist in the latter, before appearing from the bench against Belgium.

Even as the Lions of Teranga struggled going forward, Camara averaged 3.4 interceptions per 90 across 288 minutes and registered a highly-impressive 0.32 expected assists per 90 from the base of midfield.

Camara was one of the stand-out midfielders in Ligue 1 last season with Monaco, proving his World Cup was no fluke. A combative and press-resistant player with plenty of quality on the ball, Camara is equally adept at sweeping up loose balls in midfield as he is putting opponents under pressure - making 7.68 recoveries per 90 and winning possession in the final third 1.02 times per 90.

‌



View 15 Images Lamine Camara is an all-rounder in midfield whose creativity has only grown - could be be a coup for Fulham or is he already set for a top club? (Image: Machine Football)

Verdict: The best fit for that skill set turns out to be Fulham. They ranked in just the 13th percentile for dribbling and 10th for offensive duels won last season, among the weakest ball-progression numbers in the Premier League.

Camara's passing range and composure address exactly that - while he would also add much-needed steel to a high-pressing, possession-focused team such as Liverpool.

Liverpool investment explained as Jeff Bezos talks revealed after FSG statement released READ MORE :

Andoni Iraola clarifies future of two Liverpool stars linked with exits READ MORE :

Left defensive midfielder: Gustavo Puerta, 22 (Racing Santander, Colombia; True Value: £8.3m)

View 15 Images Gustavo Puerta of Colombia vs Switzerland (Image: Curtis Wong/SPP/Shutterstock)

‌



A genuine value story, Puerta was playing in Spain's Segunda Division last season, yet at 22 already ranked in the top 5% for output at that level. His playing style combines control, progression and defensive awareness.

Colombia clearly trusted him with more than a bit-part role. Puerta started every match of their World Cup campaign and was never substituted, including the full 130 minutes of their penalty-shootout defeat.

Across 519 minutes, he completed 92.4% of his passes and averaged 2.4 interceptions per 90, showing remarkable composure for a 22-year-old.

At club level, he helped Racing Santander to a league title and automatic promotion last season as their midfield controller, making a team-high 1.2 interceptions and 57.3 passes per 90, while no other Racing outfielder made more recoveries than Puerta's 6.4 per 90.

‌



Verdict: On this evidence, where would he do most good? Michael Carrick's Manchester United side ranked in just the ninth percentile for offensive duels and 18th for dribbling last season and are a side more focused on getting the ball to their creator-in-chief, Bruno Fernandes.

Puerta's calmness in possession and ability to move the ball through the lines of midfield could help with that, at a fraction of the cost of a comparable player from a bigger league.

OPINION Six standout World Cup stars who Man Utd could sign next for Michael Carrick rebuild by Tom Victor

No. 10: Fares Chaibi, 23 (Eintracht Frankfurt, Algeria; True Value: £12.9m)

View 15 Images Fares Chaibi of Algeria (Image: Xinhua/Shutterstock)

‌



Machine Football classifies Chaibi as a 'Metronomic 8', although both club and country typically use him higher up the pitch in a No. 10 role or even on the wing.

Algeria's usage of the 23-year-old only strengthened that profile. He started all four of Algeria's matches, played over 100 minutes in all of them and was never substituted, completing 88.8% of his passes despite Algeria conceding eight goals.

In the Bundesliga, Chaibi racked up nine assists for Eintracht Frankfurt last season, creating 0.55 big chances per 90 and winning possession in the final third 0.60 times per 90.

Verdict: The clearest destination for that skill set is Crystal Palace. They produced one of the weakest attacking profiles of any Premier League side last season, ranking just third for offensive duels won. Chaibi's ability to win his individual battles and convert possession into chances directly addresses that particular shortcoming.

‌



Three things the Premier League must steal from World Cup 2026 and four things it must ditch READ MORE :

2034 World Cup could be delayed until following year as FIFA face Saudi Arabia dilemma READ MORE :

Right winger: Nestory Irankunda, 20 (Watford, Australia; True Value: £13.1m)

View 15 Images Australia's Nestory Irankunda celebrates scoring his team's first goal against Türkiye (Image: Getty Images)

Still playing Championship football despite a spell at Bayern Munich after leaving Australia, Irankunda already ranks in the top 5% for both dribbling and attacking output relative to his level.

His World Cup performances showed why he is one of the most intriguing young forwards in the Machine Football database. For Australia, Irankunda scored against Turkiye, assisted against Egypt and completed the full 90 against Paraguay.

Across 285 minutes of action he won 5.7 duels per 90 — a genuinely elite physical number for a 20-year-old winger. That profile is what allows Irankunda to also play as a centre-forward, where he can call upon his combative instincts to make a nuisance of himself and unleash havoc.

‌



Irankunda's ability to take players on was on full display for Watford last season, completing 2.44 dribbles and winning 2.13 fouls per 90 in the Championship.

Verdict: On the basis of that, Newcastle looks like the obvious destination. They ranked in the 30th percentile for dribbling last season, relying heavily on crosses rather than beating defenders one-on-one.

The right-footed Irankunda could address that effectively with plenty of room still to grow - complementing the Magpies' new left-footed youngster, Bazoumana Toure, on the opposite flank.

Irankunda has been linked with a move to Sporting CP so Premier League sides would have to act quickly. Everton have also been rumoured with interest.

‌



Left winger: Malik Tillman, 23 (Bayer Leverkusen, USA; True Value: £36.6m)

View 15 Images Malik Tillman celebrates after scoring a free kick against Bosnia (Image: AP Photo/Martin Meissner)

Tillman's World Cup performances were simply too strong to leave him out.

Tillman is probably the best-known player on this list alongside Camara, and he started every USA match through to the round of 16 - scoring against Bosnia-Herzegovina and Belgium and assisting against Paraguay.

Across 415 minutes at the tournament he averaged 0.43 goals, 0.22 assists and 7.6 duels won per 90 – a dangerous combination of output and physicality rarely found together at this level which reflects Tillman's time spent as a No. 9 in Bayern's youth ranks.

‌



Tillman scored six goals from just 18 starts for Leverkusen last season, timing his box-crashing runs to perfection, and also won 51.5% of his overall duels along with an eye-catching 63.4% of his aerial ones.

View 15 Images Malik Tillman is a versatile player who can contribute defensively as well as in attack, where his box-crashing runs cause problems for defences (Image: Machine Football)

That physicality would suggest he could thrive in the Premier League, and is backed up by Tillman's 0.97 interceptions and also 0.97 instances of possession won in the final third per 90.

Verdict: There is no perfect data match here, but Brighton come closest closest. They ranked in the 26th percentile for defensive duels and 22nd for interceptions last season, a system that presses hard without always winning the ball back.

‌



Tillman could help make that press more watertight as well as offering box threat from open play, suiting how Fabian Hurzeler wants his side to play whilst adding something Brighton don't have already with his physicality and potential usefulness at set pieces.

Striker: Julian Quinones, 29 (Al Qadsiah, Mexico; True Value: £16.2m)

View 15 Images Mexico's Julian Quinones (Image: AP Photo/Fernando Llano)

Few players anywhere matched Quinones for production this year. He ranks in the top 1% globally for both attacking positioning and finishing, scoring 33 goals in 31 Saudi Pro League matches.

How translatable that would be to the Premier League, in theory at least, remains to be seen. As yet, there aren't really any other examples of Premier League clubs signing high-volume Pro League strikers to compare Quinones to.

‌



But Quinones' performances up front for Mexico at the World Cup suggest he can be effective even against elite defenders. He started all five of Mexico's World Cup matches and scored against South Africa, Czechia, Ecuador and England.

His return of 0.82 goals per 90, backed by 2.86 shots per 90, is an elite scoring rate by any standard, and he has matched or overperformed his xG in each of his two seasons in Saudi Arabia.

Verdict: Which side needs a finisher more than anyone? Tottenham ranked in just the 25th percentile for shot volume and 31st for shot quality last season. They create enough chances, but Quinones looks like the sort of striker who finishes them.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick axes five Man Utd stars as major rebuild gathers pace
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick axes five Man Utd stars as major rebuild gathers pace

Manchester United are busy sorting out transfers with a number of stars already emptied from Old Trafford

View 3 Images Michael Carrick could axe more stars (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has already approved the departures of Casemiro, Rasmus Hojlund, Jadon Sancho, Tyrell Malacia and Andre Onana. The Manchester United boss might contemplate more exits as he brings Youri Tielemans, Karl Darlow and Andrey Santos to Old Trafford.

‌



Carrick was handed the United role on a permanent basis in May and the roster of released players was announced just a month afterwards. The manager was afforded time to assess which stars he wished to keep and therefore approved all exits.

‌



Malacia, Sancho and Casemiro's deals all ran out this summer, with the latter confirming his decision in January. Meanwhile, Hojlund made his loan switch to Napoli permanent after the Serie A outfit activated his £38million release clause.

‌



Onana extended his loan spell at Trabzonspor for another campaign after helping the Super Lig club to a third-place finish and a Turkish Cup victory. This indicates that Carrick has permitted five first-team players to leave to date and with three new senior signings confirmed, the club's overhaul is really gathering pace.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

Man Utd ahead of Arsenal in Manu Kone race after opening transfer talks for £51m star READ MORE :

Following his United exit, Malacia has yet to secure another club and remains available on the free-agent market. Celtic and Napoli were previously linked with interest.

‌



Sancho has been linked with a potential comeback to Borussia Dortmund after returning to form during his loan spell there from United in 2024. Casemiro appears set to link up with Lionel Messi at Inter Miami, having also held discussions with MLS outfit LA Galaxy.

View 3 Images These five stars won't play for United this year (Image: Getty)

With these five players removed from the wage bill, freeing up a substantial £830,000, Carrick can turn his attention to further additions that will strengthen the squad. Midfielder Andrey Santos was the first arrival of the summer, signing a five-year deal worth an initial £48m.

‌



Next came a shrewd piece of business from Leeds in the shape of goalkeeper Karl Darlow, who arrived on a free transfer. The club bolstered their midfield with former Aston Villa man Youri Tielemans, who signed for £35m.

Winger Tynan Thompson has also been snapped up from Spurs and is expected to divide his time between the first team and the Under-21s. United remain keen on several targets as they press ahead with their rebuild, including Bournemouth's Alex Scott.

View 3 Images Alex Scott is a main target for United (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

Article continues below

The club received an apparent boost in their pursuit of Scott this week, with the understanding that he is their primary midfield priority. Scott has turned down a new contract at Bournemouth, which has undoubtedly improved United's prospects of securing his signature this summer.

The Cherries expect the midfielder to stay put this season, but Carrick remains firmly interested. United are expected to face stiff competition from Arsenal and Chelsea for the midfielder, though his refusal to sign a new contract suggests he may be open to leaving.

Sports.title: Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race
Sports.content:
Alex Scott transfer twist as Bournemouth star ‘keen’ on rivals amid Arsenal and Man Utd race

Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott's transfer stance has now emerged following Chelsea's initial £64million bid, with Manchester United and Arsenal also admirers

View Image Alex Scott is thought to be keen on a move to Chelsea after their initial bid was rejected (Image: James Marsh/Shutterstock)

Alex Scott is reportedly pushing to secure a move to Chelsea after the Blues saw a £64million bid rejected. The midfielder is subject of interest from Arsenal, Manchester United, Manchester City and Tottenham.

‌



However, Scott is keen to join Chelsea, according to the Standard, and has no intention of committing to an extension at Bournemouth. The former Bristol City midfielder has two years left on his current deal on the south coast.

‌



Despite his determination to secure a summer switch, Bournemouth insist he is not for sale and remain hopeful of convincing him to agree fresh terms. The Cherries offered Scott a new contract in March, but talks have stalled, with the Guernsey‑born midfielder focused on leaving.

‌



Arsenal issue statement and confirm extent of worrying William Saliba injury problem READ MORE :

5 transfers you missed during the World Cup including £47m Chelsea move and Arsenal bargain READ MORE :

Scott featured in all but three Premier League fixtures for the Cherries last season. He contributed to the club's sixth-place finish in the top division and secured their spot in the Europa League.

In addition, Scott received his maiden England senior call-up last November, although he didn't feature in any matches.

He was selected as one of five players - alongside Rio Ngumoha, Jason Steele, Josh King and Ethan Nwaneri - who would link up with the Three Lions squad for the preparation camp ahead of the World Cup.

‌



Meanwhile, Chelsea kept a watchful eye on Scott and his development throughout last season.

With central midfield firmly in Xabi Alonso's sights as an area requiring improvement, the Blues have stepped up their pursuit of Scott, lodging a £64m bid - though Bournemouth were quick to send it packing.

Prior to the move for Scott, Alonso had hoped to reunite with Granit Xhaka, with Chelsea submitting an £8m offer to Sunderland for the 33 year old last month, only for it to be promptly knocked back.

‌



FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Blues initially received positive signals from the Switzerland international regarding a potential switch to Stamford Bridge, and a second offer was being mulled over - however, Xhaka subsequently pledged his allegiance to the Black Cats, prompting the west Londoners to walk away from talks.

Chelsea also harbour a longstanding interest in Adam Wharton, sources say, with the Crystal Palace midfielder's future at Selhurst Park far from certain.

Article continues below

The Blues have monitored Wharton's progression closely at their London rivals over the past couple of seasons, though in a central midfield market, one that has seen Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes cost almost £100m, the England international is unlikely to come at a bargain price.

Meanwhile, United have added Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow to Michael Carrick's squad at Old Trafford in this transfer window.

Sports.title: Salt stars as Fire end eight-match Hundred losing streak against Brave
Sports.content:
Phil Salt weathered a bowling storm from England fast bowler Jofra Archer as the Welsh Fire captain led his side to a six-wicket victory over Southern Brave in The Hundred.

The win snapped Fire's eight-match losing streak against Brave, with Salt carrying the team over the line in dramatic fashion.

After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire found themselves needing 14 runs off 10 balls at the end of their innings, and Salt, alongside Asa Tribe, showed his composure to whittle down the tally.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After being set a target of 135 to win, Fire's Phil Salt whittled down the run chase and secured victory with a six

Salt, who struck an unbeaten 47 off 37 deliveries, found himself on strike with only four runs left to win from three deliveries, and the captain swept away Chris Jordan for a big six to wrap up the victory.

"The conditions weren't easy. It was a good toss for us to win and chasing the target, we knew what it was," Salt told Sky Sports.

"We were electric in the field. There was some real good catching on display. We got off the rope well today. Bowling-wise, we put the ball in the right areas. Did we do it for long enough? Were we smart enough? That's one for the coaches."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player David Miller (44) and Thomas Rew (41) struck the highest individual scores for the Brave

Brave started slowly, with Sam Cook first snaring Jamie Smith for three runs, before Marco Jansen had Ben McKinney for four.

Thomas Rew (41) and David Miller (44) steadied the ship, before Jansen hit back with his second of the match to dismiss the former off 30 balls.

Archer came to the crease but was run out in the most bizarre of circumstances. Miller had struck a ball to Jansen at cover, and the England seamer had attempted to get up for a single, but his batting partner sent him back, turning in a circle in the middle of the wicket as Fire made the pair pay for their miscommunication.

Salt and Matthew Short arrived at the crease after the intermission, with Short bringing up a score of 20 before being caught out at extra cover by Dan Worrall.

Worrall was back in on the action again, combining with Smith to dismiss England legend Joe Root for 15 runs.

Image: Former England captain Joe Root was dismissed for 15 runs after he was run out by Dan Worrall and Jamie Smith

Rachin Ravindra arrived at the crease, and it was here that the Fire kicked on, with he and Salt bringing up an impressive partnership of 49 runs off 27 balls.

"It's great to play a role in a partnership," Ravindra said to Sky Sports. "Communication was key out there between us. Salty played well out there. It wasn't such a free-flowing T20 wicket as we're used to seeing.

"He supported me greatly during that partnership, and it's great to see the skipper finish it off at the end.

"We're all used to seeing that free-flowing Phil Salt, aren't we? The comms were mostly just about hitting good cricket shots, trusting our positions, hitting the gaps hard and running hard, and the boundaries would come.

"Salty is such a special player but showed his maturity and leadership to keep us accountable ball after ball."

What's next?

Thursday's Hundred double-header comes from Lord's in London as London Spirit take on Manchester Super Giants. The women's game starts at 2.45pm, with the men's match due to commence from 6.30pm. Catch both fixtures live on Sky Sports and on YouTube. Watch The Hundred and more contract-free on NOW

Sports.title: Saliba out for 'extended period' with back injury
Sports.content:
Arsenal have confirmed William Saliba will be out for an extended period with a back injury.

However, the France international central defender is not expected to have surgery, according to a club statement.

Saliba was substituted in the 30th minute of France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain.

"William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition," the Arsenal statement reads.

"Subsequent specialist reviews on William's return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

"Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.

Image: Arsenal's win rate drops to 47.6 per cent without Saliba

"William's rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

"Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible."

Saliba's injury comes after other key players Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Odegaard struggled with fitness issues last season. Rice and Saka had to then manage injury problems whilst playing at the World Cup.

All players who were at the tournament receive a mandatory three weeks off after their country's involvement ended before they need to report for pre-season training.

Arsenal's first of four pre-season games is on August 1 against Girona, followed by the Community Shield against Manchester City in Cardiff on August 16. They begin their Premier League title defence on Friday August 21 at home to Coventry, live on Sky Sports.

Who could fill in Saliba's absence

In more positive news for Arsenal, Ben White is back in pre-season training after his knee injury sustained in May.

The England international sustained the injury during the crucial 1-0 win over West Ham in the Gunners' third-from-last game of the 2025/26 Premier League season. He was subsequently ruled out for the Champions League final against Paris Saint-Germain.

Jurrien Timber however is still rehabilitating from the groin injury that kept him out of the World Cup. The defender said he is "hopefully back soon".

Cristhian Mosquera and Riccardo Calafiori are also back for pre-season and can fill in at centre-back if required.

Piero Hincapie is expected to return to training within the next week after Ecuador's Round of 32 elimination from the World Cup. Saliba's partner in crime Gabriel Magalhaes is also expected to link up with the rest of the squad soon.

Sports.title: New signings shine, absentees and exciting youth - Spurs kickstart pre-season
Sports.content:
Tottenham made a winning start to pre-season with a 1-0 victory over newly-promoted League One side MK Dons at Hotspur Way.

The win came courtesy of a stunning volleyed goal from new Spurs signing Mateus Fernandes.

He was one of three summer arrivals on display as Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi used 21 players across the 90 minutes.

Here, Sky Sports assesses Spurs' first pre-season friendly…

How Spurs lined up... First Half: Kinsky; Gray, Takai, Davies, Kyerematen; Tonali, Fernandes; Solomon, Gallagher, Tel; Solanke.

Second Half: Dubravka; Kyerematen, Hardy, T Hall, Bryne; Yang, Donley, Williams-Barnett, Moore; Scarlett, Richarlison.

Fernandes shines

"It was my favourite goal of my career by a mile."

Just three minutes into his first Spurs game, Fernandes made the dream start to life in north London.

The midfielder, who joined from West Ham for £85m, expertly kept his eye on a high ball cleared at a corner to superbly smash a first-time volleyed screamer from the edge of the box to give Spurs an early lead.

What a way to introduce yourself to Spurs fans, whose excitement levels will have increased watching his 45-minute display before he was taken off as part of De Zerbi's wholesale half-time changes.

Fernandes' willingness to play forward passes, which did not always come off, was a particular positive considering the lack of creativity last season.

Tonali and Dubravka make solid debuts

Fernandes may have outshone midfield partner Tonali, but the Italy international kept things ticking over in midfield nicely.

Plenty of absentees in win

Kinsky's promotion to first choice and Dubravka's arrival has put Guglielmo Vicario's future in serious doubt, and it was no surprise to see the Juventus and Napoli target missing against MK Dons.

His fellow Italy international, Destiny Udogie, was also absent, but Spurs' first-choice left-back was part of a group of players watching the game.

Teenage kicks

With plenty of senior players missing, it gave the youngsters a chance to impress.

Sports.title: Villa agree deal to sign Garnacho...but it's complicated
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have agreed a deal to sign Alejandro Garnacho from Chelsea.

The arrangement is for a loan with a conditional obligation to buy, which is easily achievable.

The total package, including the loan fee, is understood to meet Chelsea's valuation.

Sky Sports News has been reporting Chelsea wanted £42.6m for the winger.

Garnacho joined Chelsea last summer from Manchester United for £40m.
