Sports.title: Troy Deeney: Amazing Erling Haaland is a freak, but he’s not in all-time top 10 Premier League strikers
Sports.content:
Troy Deeney: Amazing Erling Haaland is a freak, but he’s not in all-time top 10 Premier League strikers

Erling Haaland might have broken many Premier League scoring records - but he's still not one of its all-time great strikers.

That's the opinion of former top-flight forward Troy Deeney, who doesn't have the Manchester City superstar in his top 10 Premier League frontmen.



5 Deeney doesn't have Haaland in his best-ever strikers despite his stunning stats Credit: Getty

Haaland turned 26 on Tuesday, celebrating his birthday just a few weeks before the 2026/27 campaign gets started.

After a successful first-ever World Cup with Norway, the forward turns his attention back to domestic football.

And there's no doubt that he will be eyeing more records.

Haaland has made an incredible amount of history since joining Man City in 2022, breaking new boundaries every year.



He has the title of being the fastest player ever to reach a tally of 10, 20, 30, 40, 50 and 100 goals in the Premier League.

The Norwegian has also become the fastest player to reach 100 goal involvements in fewer than 100 league games (94).



As well as that, the City talisman has the record for the most goals ever scored in a single Premier League season (36).

It doesn't stop there either, with Haaland the only player ever to score a hat-trick in three consecutive home league games.



And he has another amazing record too, being the first player to score 50+ goals in a top-flight season in England since 1931.

In total, Haaland has scored 112 Premier League goals in just 132 games, but Deeney doesn't think he sits with the greats...

5 Haaland has made an incredible amount of history in just four years

Is Haaland the best ever striker in the Premier League?

Drive host Andy Goldstein read out all of those stats that Haaland has managed to achieve across the last four years.



And he asked whether he is the best ever seen in the top-flight, with Deeney replying: "Not yet no. All of the stuff there is brilliant.

"When you start to have this conversation, it's always good to say that he is a freak... I also think there's still a long way to go.

"My top five at the moment is: Thierry Henry at one, Wayne Rooney at two, Alan Shearer at three, Andy Cole at four and then fifth, it depends.

"Fifth is always changing... it goes between Harry Kane, Jermain Defoe, Sergio Aguero, Robbie Fowler, Luis Suarez.



"I've got ten... Haaland's not in there, not yet, no."

5 Deeney has Henry as the greatest Premier League striker of all time Credit: Getty

5 He also thinks City icon Aguero is above Haaland in the all-time list Credit: Getty

Goldstein then questioned: "He's tops every single list and he's not in your top 10 Premier League strikers?"

And Deeney went on to explain: "A lot of it for me is about feeling as well, what those players made you feel when you watched them.



"Henry, you watched him and you were like 'Wow', you'd never seen anyone that quick, he had that finish into the bottom corner.

"Rooney, as a kid, he was one of the best players I'd ever seen, he could do it all... Shearer, it's obviously goals.

"Cole is the most disrespected striker in Premier League history. He's never in anybody else's top 10... he scored over 180 goals.

"Defoe did it for so many years, Aguero was unbelievable... I think [I'd put him above Haaland]."



5 Deeney wants Haaland to drag City to the title this season to prove he should be in the top 10 Credit: Getty

What more has Haaland got to do to get in?

So, if Haaland isn't in the top 10 greatest ever Premier League strikers now, how does he make his way into the list?

Deeney said: "I think this season is going to be really interesting.

"The seasons he's been at City, they have been unbelievable anyway and he's been a piece to that, an additional piece.

"It'll be interesting now they're not favourites to win it. Can he carry the team a little bit?"



He added: "I'd like to see him drag this team forward... when he played against Arsenal, against Gabriel, I was like 'wow'.

"He dragged the team to win that game, I'd like to see that more."

Sports.title: William Saliba injury latest as Arsenal give fresh update on star defender
Sports.content:
William Saliba will be out for an 'extended period' with a back injury but will not require surgery.

Arsenal confirmed the news in an update on Wednesday after the star defender went off injured during France's World Cup semi-final defeat to Spain last week.



4 Saliba is set for a extended period out of action after picking up the injury in the World Cup semi-final Credit: Getty

While it's not stated how long Saliba will be sidelined for, the recommendation for him to not have surgery will be a boost for the Gunners.

It had been reported in French media that he could be out until December prior to Arsenal's announcement.

Arsenal update on Saliba injury

"William Saliba has returned to us from World Cup duty, where he played an integral role in France reaching the semi-finals of the competition," Arsenal said in a statement.



"Subsequent specialist reviews on William’s return to London this week have confirmed that he has suffered a back injury which will require a period of rehabilitation.

"Extensive assessments have concluded that surgery is not recommended, but William should now commence a managed recovery programme.



"William’s rehabilitation will commence immediately, with continual management of his injury, and he is expected to be out of action for an extended period.

"Everyone is fully focused on supporting William to ensure he is back to full fitness as soon as possible."



The Arsenal defender had been following a modified training programme throughout the World Cup in an attempt to manage his back pain.

However, the 25-year-old could manage just 30 minutes of last Tuesday's 2-0 semi-final loss.

French journalist and regular talkSPORT contributor Julien Laurens claimed following the injury that Saliba could be heard saying, 'My back is gone'.

4 It appears Saliba's injury is not as bad as first feared Credit: Getty



How did Saliba's injury occur?

The incident during the game occurred with Saliba under no immediate pressure.

Saliba went down and signalled to the bench to be replaced with France already 1-0 down to the 2010 world champions.

The centre-back slowly walked off the pitch, helped by two members of the team’s medical staff.

Deschamps turned to Crystal Palace centre-back Maxence Lacroix as his replacement alongside Dayot Upamecano.



But things went from bad to worse for France as Tottenham's Pedro Porro doubled Spain's lead in the 58th minute and booked their place in the final, where they will face Argentina following their dramatic 2-1 comeback win over England.

Saliba was a key figure for the Gunners in the 2025/26 season, helping the club to their first Premier League title in 22 years.

4 Saliba looked emotional as he made his way off the pitch in France's defeat to Spain Credit: Getty

The Paris-born star had been just as crucial for France en route to the World Cup and during the tournamen, despite nursing a back issue.



He missed the final group stage match against Norway in a bid to preserve his fitness and with France already having booked their place in the last-32.

His back complaint was one that was closely monitored and managed by France's medical team.

Saliba recently admitted he had been playing with the problem throughout Arsenal's Champions League tussles and Premier League title run-in.

“I’ve had some minor niggles for several months,” Saliba said during the early stages of the World Cup.



“I’ve been gritting my teeth because there was the Champions League and the Premier League.

4 Saliba has featured in at least 50 games for Arsenal in each of the last three campaigns Credit: Getty

"But the coaching staff are handling it very well. The World Cup comes around only once every four years, so you’ve got to grit your teeth.

"I’m not at 100 percent, but there are plenty of players who aren’t at 100 per cent either. You can’t make excuses.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham in World Cup Team of the Tournament as Spain stars suffer shock omissions
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi, Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham in World Cup Team of the Tournament as Spain stars suffer shock omissions

Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon must be wondering what more he had to do to make it into FIFA's World Cup Team of the Tournament.

The team, officially dubbed the 'Dream XI', was voted on by fans across the world.

5 Simon was forced to make only 14 saves across the tournament Credit: Getty

Simon was beaten just once throughout the entire competition as Spain went on to win their first World Cup in 16 years.

The only time Simon conceded came during Spain's 2-1 win over Belgium in the quarter-finals when Charles De Ketelaere headed home from close range.

Simon's seven clean sheets from eight games earned him the Golden Glove, which is awarded to the goalkeeper who concedes the fewest goals at the World Cup.

Which goalkeeper beat Unai Simon to the Team of the Tournament?

However, the accolade was not good enough to earn a spot in the team of the tournament.

Instead, it was Cape Verde glovesman Vozinha who was named to the team.

The 40-year-old became an instant cult hero when he helped the African island nation keep an improbable clean sheet against Spain in their World Cup opener.

Vozinha's stunning exploits between the sticks made him a viral hit on social media.

He boasted nearly 40,000 Instagram followers before the tournament but that figure has risen to a whopping 29.5million.

On the pitch, Vozinha ended the World Cup with 18 saves made, the eighth-most across all goalkeepers.

Paraguay's Orlando Gill was the busiest of all the World Cup goalkeepers, making a whopping 28 saves.

Which defenders made the Team of the Tournament?

The defensive four in the team of the tournament was comprised of Marc Cucurella, Dayot Upamecano, Lisandro Martinez and Pedro Porro.

5 Despite playing a part in Tottenham coming 17th, Porro ensured Spain wouldn't have similar misery Credit: Getty

Cucurella and Porro were part of the dominant Spanish back line that shipped just one goal.

Yet there was no room for Aymeric Laporte or Pau Cubarsi, who formed a dominant partnership at centre-back for La Roja.

Adding to the weight of Cubarsi's snub was the fact he was named the Young Player of the Tournament.

Martinez started all but one of Argentina's eight games at the World Cup, but his tournament ended in cruel fashion as he was forced off with an injury during the final.

Upamecano helped France reach the semi-finals, where they ran into a rampant Spain.

Prior to their semi-final clash, France had conceded just two goals in six games.

5 Argentina conceded six times in four games with Martinez at the back Credit: Getty

Which midfielders made the Team of the Tournament?

Although the goalkeeper and defence may have left room for debate, there would be little argument for the midfield three, which was comprised of Rodri, Jude Bellingham and Michael Olise.

Rodri was awarded the Golden Ball, given to the best player of the tournament, thanks to his exploits for Spain.

Olise finished the tournament with seven assists, one shy of equalling fellow Frenchman Raymond Kopa's record which has stood since 1958.

As for Bellingham, his seven goals from midfield for England placed him third in the Golden Boot race.

Of those seven goals, four came in the Three Lions' victories over Mexico and Norway in the round of 16 and quarter-final respectively, underlining Bellingham's propensity to step up in the big moments.

Which forwards made the Team of the Tournament?

Similarly to the midfield, the front three largely picked themselves.

5 Kylian Mbappe shattered goal records at this World Cup and won't be slowing down any time soon Credit: Getty

Golden Boot winner Kylian Mbappe, who scored a staggering ten goals and contributed four assists, was a shoe-in for the team of the tournament.

The French skipper's haul also made him the World Cup record goalscorer, with a whopping 22 goals scored across three tournaments.

As was Lionel Messi who, at age 39, proved that there was plenty of magic left in his legs.

Messi inspired Argentina to a third World Cup final in four tournaments on the back of his eight goals and four assists.

Norway's Erling Haaland completed the team of the tournament having scored seven goals.

Sports.title: Ipswich Town finalising move for Celtic and World Cup star in £10m deal
Sports.content:
Ipswich Town finalising move for Celtic and World Cup star in £10m deal

Ipswich Town are formalising a move for Celtic forward Daizen Maeda, talkSPORT understands.

The total package is set to be worth £10million.

2 Maeda has proved tremendous value for money with Celtic Credit: Getty



Maeda would join Ipswich following a trophy-laden four-and-a-half years at Celtic Park.

Since his arrival in December 2021, the 28-year-old has won ten pieces of silverware.

Of those ten, five were Celtic's Scottish Premiership triumphs, along with three Scottish Cups and two Scottish League Cups.

On an individual basis, Maeda produced his best displays in the 2024/25 campaign as he bagged 33 goals in 51 appearances across all competitions.



His brilliance that season was recognised by being named the PFA Scotland Players' Player of the Year, Celtic Player of the Year and an inclusion in the PFA Scotland Team of the Year.

In total, Maeda has scored 79 goals for the Hoops from 212 appearances.



Maeda is also fresh off four appearances for Japan at the World Cup.

The forward started three of Japan's four matches, contributing one assist.

Ipswich's hectic summer

Maeda's mooted arrival continues what has been a busy summer for the Tractor Boys following their promotion from the Championship.



Ipswich will go into the new campaign with a new manager for the first time since December 2021 after Kieran McKenna chose to step down.

2 O'Neil is desperate to avoid an instant return to the Championship with Ipswich Credit: AFP

He was swiftly replaced by Gary O'Neil, who was plucked from Ligue 1 side Strasbourg.

Following O'Neil's arrival, Ipswich have brought in a string of players, including striker Emersonn from Toulouse for a club-record £26.6million.



Leicester City forward Abdul Fatawu is another key addition, as is Moroccan centre-back Issa Diop from Fulham.

Cedric Kipre and Chuba Akpom also returned to Ipswich on a permanent basis after a successful loan spell last term.

Ipswich begin their Premier League campaign on August 22 against Sunderland.

Sports.title: Leicester explore sale of club ten years after 5000/1 Premier League win
Sports.content:
Leicester's owners are reportedly exploring the sale of the club, a decade on from their Premier League title success.

According to the Financial Times, the Foxes' King Power owners have brought in investment bankers at Citigroup to help sound out potential buyers.



3 Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha took over as Leicester chairman in 2018 Credit: AFP

Meanwhile, Sky Sports news report that an unnamed Middle Eastern firm are interested in buying the club, whose portfolio has been shown to a number of potential investors by their advisors.

Should a change in ownership materialise, this would bring an end to one of football's most remarkable ownership stories.

End of an era?

King Power's billionaire founder, Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, took over at Leicester in 2010, with the team mid-table in the Championship.



In 2014, they won promotion to the Premier League, before enjoying arguably the game's greatest fairy tale story two years later.

Under Claudio Ranieri, the Foxes pulled off one of the greatest shocks in sporting history as they lifted the league title.



The club enjoyed continued success in the years that followed, reaching the quarter-finals of the Champions League in 2017.

But tragedy struck in 2018 when Srivaddhanaprabha died in a helicopter crash outside the team’s stadium, with his son Aiyawatt - known as Top - subsequently taking control of the club.



While Leicester tasted FA Cup glory in 2021, things have taken a turn for the worse at the King Power Stadium since then.

The Foxes suffered relegation from the Premier League in 2023, before bouncing back the following season under Enzo Maresca.

Their return didn't last long though, and they were relegated again in 2025, before disaster struck in the recently-concluded 2025/26 campaign.

3 The football world fell in love with Leicester after their most improbable title success Credit: AFP or licensors



A decade on from their 5000/1 Premier League title success, the East Midlands outfit finished second-bottom in the Championship, condemning them to League One.

Financial woes

Their relegation came amid a backdrop of ongoing financial issues behind the scenes.

Leicester were deducted six points in February after being found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules for the 2023/24 season.

They breached the EFL Profit and Sustainability Rules (P&S Rules) by reporting losses of £201.9million in the three-year period between 2022 and 2024.



Accounts released this year showed the club lost £71.1million during the 2024/25 Premier League campaign.

In 2025, Leicester's owners wiped £124m of shareholder loans to the club, which converted the debt to equity.

Unsurprisingly, the Foxes' continued financial woes off the pitch and struggles on it has led to chairman Srivaddhanaprabha facing huge criticism from fans, after years of questionable decisions.

3 The King Power ownership is plain to see at Leicester, with their stadium bearing its name Credit: Getty



The current ownership has relocated the club into a multi-million-pound training ground in Seagrave and had explored expanding the current stadium capacity to 40,000.

However, plans for the latter have been put on hold following relegation, with the ground set to remain in its 32,000-seater form.

King Power’s core business has been hit by a drop in visitors to Thailand in the wake of the coronavirus pandemic, especially from China.

Airports of Thailand said in October it had agreed to renegotiate some of the company’s retail concession contracts.

Sports.title: New Rangers boss Derek McInnes to miss first three games in dugout as he’s slapped with ban
Sports.content:
New Rangers boss Derek McInnes to miss first three games in dugout as he’s slapped with ban

New Rangers boss Derek McInnes has copped a three-match touchline ban following comments he made about Scottish officials.

McInnes was hit with a four-game ban, with one suspended, for criticising the decision to award Celtic a late penalty against Motherwell towards the end of last season.

2 McInnes was left seething after Celtic were given a controversial penalty Credit: Getty

The new 'Gers boss was in charge of Hearts at the time, who were locked in a tussle for the Scottish Premiership title with Celtic but ultimately fell short.

Against Motherwell, Celtic were awarded a penalty in the ninth minute of second-half stoppage time for a contentious handball, which they ultimately converted to win the game.

What did McInnes say to land him in hot water?

McInnes labelled referee John Beaton's decision to point to spot, following a recommendation from video assistant Andrew Dallas, as 'quite disgusting.'

"I shouldn't be commenting on another game, but having seen that, it feels like us against everybody," McInnes added.

Had Celtic not beaten Motherwell, Hearts would have won their first Scottish Premiership in 66 years.

Instead, the Hoops' win over Motherwell had them just one point behind Hearts going into the final day.

As it transpired, Celtic broke Hearts' spirits when Daizen Maeda gave them a 2-1 lead in the 87th minute before Callum Osmand put the cherry on top in the eighth minute of second-half stoppage time to spark a chaotic pitch invasion.

The devastating manner of defeat had Hearts players in tears upon their return from Celtic Park.

Following Hearts' devastating end to the season, McInnes joined Rangers after predecessor Danny Rohl moved to RB Salzburg.

McInnes' switch to Rangers reunited him with striker Lawrence Shankland, who had joined the Scottish giants from Hearts only weeks earlier.

2 McInnes twisted the knife further into Hearts as he followed Shankland to Ibrox Credit: Getty

Which Rangers games will McInnes miss?

The ban means McInnes will be absent from Rangers' Scottish Premiership season opener away to Dundee United on July 31.

He will also miss Hibernian's visit to Ibrox on August 9 and Rangers' second round clash in the Scottish League Cup against a yet-to-be-named opponent over the weekend of August 15-16.

However, McInnes will be available to take charge of Rangers' Europa League qualifiers against Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok.

McInnes' side will make the trip to Poland for the first leg of their third qualifying round tie on August 6 before contesting the second leg at Ibrox on August 13.

The 55-year-old's first competitive match as Rangers boss in a Scottish competition falls on August 22 against St Mirren.

Sports.title: Man City confident of reaching deal for World Cup sensation Ayyoub Bouaddi
Sports.content:
Manchester City are increasingly hopeful of signing Lille midfielder Ayyoub Bouaddi, talkSPORT understands.

Bouaddi, who was a breakout star for Morocco at the World Cup, has been a target for multiple Premier League giants this summer.



4 City are confident they can complete the signing of Bouaddi this summer Credit: Getty

The teenage sensation had previously held talks with Arsenal and Liverpool, while Chelsea were among those tracking him.

However, it's Man City who believe they are close to a deal, with Lille understood to be wanting £85.3million for their star.

And it is believed that City will not to be loaning Bouaddi back to the Ligue 1 side to continue his development.



This comes after Lille made it clear that they preferred to delay a transfer of the 18-year-old by a year.

Good to Bouadd

The French side are prepared to sell him, but have been offering a discounted deal if clubs were open to a loan back or pre-agreement.



If City were to let Bouaddi stay with his current team for another year, they could get a deal done for £68.2m instead.

But that doesn't seem like the case, with Enzo Maresca and co. wanting the midfielder to join straight away and be part of the squad.



talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs revealed on July 1: "This is a fascinating transfer story because Lille are prepared to sell, but they heavily favour a deal for 2027, clubs, and Manchester City, have shown they are willing to at least discuss this."

"It's €80m [£68.2m] at the moment, but could come down for those that say to Lille a loan back or pre-agreement," he added.

"It's €100m [£85.3m] for other clubs that want an immediate transfer, so that's going to be one to watch."

4 Bouaddi starred for Morocco at the World Cup and dominated against Brazil in the 1-1 draw Credit: Getty



4 The teenagers started in five matches in North America

Bouaddi's brilliant summer

Man City are set to move for Bouaddi following his incredible World Cup campaign, which saw him catch the eye.

He started every game but one for Morocco at the tournament in North America.

His performance against Brazil instantly had fans in awe, as he stood out against the South American giants.



Bouaddi had the most touches (88), won the most duels (11) and completed the most successful passes in the opposition’s half (30).

His 60 completed passes also made him the second youngest player to complete over 50 passes in a World Cup match in 60 years.

And he would go on to impress again against Scotland, the Netherlands and Canada before struggling against France.

4 Bouaddi could end up being Man City's next midfield arrival after Anderson Credit: Shutterstock Editorial



But Bouaddi remains one of the most sought-after midfielders on the planet, with City hoping to get a deal over the line.

Maresca, who is set for his first campaign in charge, is looking to bolster his midfield after losing Bernardo Silva.

He has already secured the £116m signing of Elliot Anderson, but Bouaddi may also join the talented ranks.

City have signed Anderson, Jeremy Monga, Pierce Charles and Mathys Detourbet so far this summer.

Sports.title: 'Every time I was in the middle, I saw my average drop... it was disheartening': JAMIE SMITH on his horror Ashes, repaying England's faith and the 'fantastic' coach changing his game
Sports.content:
Jamie Smith wants to use the Hundred to reignite his England white-ball career – and plans to ensure his Test average heads back in the right direction after a difficult few months in which both his batting and his wicketkeeping have been under scrutiny. Smith has not played any limited-overs international cricket since struggling in New Zealand before the Ashes, while he has averaged just 21 in Tests since his stunning double of 184 not out and 88 against India at Edgbaston in July 2025. But he regards his move to Southern Brave, his third Hundred franchise in three years, as a chance both for a fresh start and to impress England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum, sacked as Test coach but in the pink after T20 and ODI series wins over India. ‘My goals have always been to play three formats for England,’ Smith tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘I’ve had a little taste of it, and the Hundred is always a great opportunity to go out and do well against some of the best players in the world and use it as a springboard.’ Smith has played only five T20s, mainly because England have a settled and destructive opening pair in Phil Salt and Jos Buttler. But his 19 ODIs have produced just three fifties and an average of 21. ‘It just wasn’t consistent enough,’ he says. ‘I had a couple of decent enough innings, but didn’t make them count. I can’t complain with the opportunity I was given. It’s trying to learn from that.’ Jamie Smith endured a difficult Ashes Down Under last winter, in a series he admits was 'disheartening' But the wicketkeeper is intent on repaying England's faith in him, and rediscovering his best form But his main goal, ahead of next month’s three-match series against Pakistan, is to repay the selectors’ faith after they moved him above Ben Stokes up to No 6 in the Test side against New Zealand. He describes his series as ‘disjointed’, having made a crucial 39 in a low-scoring first Test at Lord’s before missing the second at the Oval because of paternity leave. In the decider at Trent Bridge, his well-paced second-innings 60 came too late to save England as the Bazball era ended in smoke and flames. But he appreciated his promotion. ‘It was a confidence-booster, especially after a disappointing Ashes,’ he says. ‘I felt like every time I was walking out to the middle, I was seeing my average drop. When you’re not playing well, it’s quite disheartening. ‘That’s something I’d be looking to improve on, trying to push that up as much as possible. There’s no reason why I can’t go to No 6 and have success. I know it’d be a good effort to go back to the standards I set at the start. But if I can go a little bit further towards pushing it back in the right direction, that’d be nice.’ Smith, whose average has slipped from 58 after that Edgbaston Test to just under 40, faced criticism during the Ashes for his demeanour behind the stumps, especially from former England wicketkeeper Matt Prior, who felt he was too quiet. ‘I understand people’s opinions,’ says Smith. ‘You want to do the best you can, but I think the thing for me is trying to put my own stamp on it. I don’t think I’d be changing too much.’

Your browser does not support iframes.

It’s why he has parked the captaincy ambitions he once harboured at Surrey. ‘I wouldn’t say it necessarily is for me – not with my personality. I’m very relaxed and enjoy the way things are going now, and playing off other people. I’m happy to play the supporting role.’ Smith says he will miss McCullum’s Test coaching after feeling supported by him on his entry to the team two years ago, but has enjoyed working closely with the former England wicketkeeper Sarah Taylor at a time when every mistake behind the stumps is accompanied by social-media cries of ‘Ben Foakes wouldn’t have dropped that’. ‘Sarah’s been fantastic,’ he says. ‘She brings a lot of energy to the group, not just for me, and she’s always willing to work at things and chat them through. ‘It’s disappointing when you drop a couple of catches and the same sort of things crop up about your keeping. 'But I felt like overall I was keeping a lot better. It’s frustrating that they’re the things that get brought up.’ ‘She's been fantastic,’ says Smith of Sarah Taylor (pictured). ‘She brings a lot of energy to the group, not just for me, and she’s always willing to work at things and chat them through' Smith showed immense promise in the early stages of his international career - now it's time to build on it The pressure grew against New Zealand, whose own wicketkeeper, Tom Blundell, provided a masterclass in standing up to the stumps, keeping Harry Brook and Joe Root tethered to the crease. Once England had left out Ollie Robinson after Lord’s, their bowlers were generally too quick for Smith to mirror the tactics. He says it felt ‘out of my comfort zone’, but adds: ‘It’s definitely something we’ll be working on.’ Smith has just turned 26, but has already established himself as one of the cleanest strikers in the English game. His international strike-rates are all formidable: 73 in Tests, 112 in ODIs and 194 in T20s. If he can get his other numbers heading in the right direction, there may be no stopping him.

Sports.title: 'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry
Sports.content:
'I can't wear high heels too often... my feet are my money-makers!': Britain's 'sexy and aggressive' sprinter AMY HUNT reveals how 'radical confidence' helped her gatecrash world's elite - and her love of 14th-century Italian poetry

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Amy Hunt is waiting for her mum, Claire, to arrive on the train from Newark to London.

‘We always enjoy a leisurely ladies' lunch when we’re here,’ she explains, putting down her Gucci handbag and sipping on a double espresso in the Daily Mail Sport offices in Kensington.

‘Sometimes it needs to be a quick Wagamama but if it’s Mum then I like to treat her. I’m now in a position where I’m lucky enough to be able to spoil my parents and really take care of them. I like fine dining. I like to give her a boujie experience and make her feel all lovely.

‘It wasn’t easy raising two incredibly sporty, high-achieving daughters. My mum would be at cricket practice at Trent Bridge with my sister (who was in Nottinghamshire's academy) and my dad would be with me at track practice. My legs run really fast and because of that I can now give my parents the life I want them to have.’

Winning a silver medal in the 200metres at last year’s World Athletics Championships has opened plenty of doors for England’s latest track star.

The 24-year-old will compete in the 100m and 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight, the latest chapter in her blossoming career which was turbo-boosted when she described herself as 'sexy and aggressive' after that runners-up finish in Tokyo.

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her choice of words – she also said you can be 'an academic badass and a track goddess at the same time' – propelled her from the back pages to the front.

British sprint star Amy Hunt, photographed in the Daily Mail Sport studios

Hunt graduated from the University of Cambridge with an English literature degree in 2023 but student halls are a thing of the past. Here in London, the Hunts are booked into the suite at the luxury hotel Kimpton Fitzroy – one of model David Gandy’s favourites – and a spot of shopping is on the cards, too.

‘We went to the Saatchi gallery last time we were here,' Hunt adds. 'They had an exhibition on flowers, with some William Morris prints. I’ve lived abroad in Padova (Italy) for three years now so I don’t get to see her as often as I would like. Spending time together in the UK is a joyful rarity.

'Mum manages antiques fairs. We have the same enjoyment for beautiful, material things. If there’s time, then we might go to Liberty's (department store) and have a wander around.

‘Winning a world individual medal definitely puts you in new rooms and new conversations. We don’t get the same financial support as other sports but we’re in the lucky position where we get paid more than niche Olympic sports like pentathlon.

‘Every sport is chasing the PR jump that F1 had (through the Netlflix documentary Drive to Survive) and there are always new initiatives coming in to try and make track big. We train in Italy so I have to say no to a lot of things. Vogue parties, movie premieres, opportunities to fly to Goodwood in a helicopter...

‘Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it. We work in such fine margins. My feet and my ankles and my legs are my money-makers, essentially.

'They’re quite susceptible to minor changes. Even when I get a new pair of spikes, sometimes I get blisters. That can have a big knock-on effect on one week of training.

‘This is so gross but my two big toenails had to be removed in Tokyo and then I got blisters on the end of both toes. Before every single race, my coach was having to tape up my toes so they weren’t bleeding everywhere. We were in a very hot, muggy climate and if they get infected, then that can have a big knock-on effect. It’s not all glamorous parties and holidays.’

Hunt's confidence, her glamorous look and her eloquence have propelled her from the back pages to the front

She won silver in the 200m at last year’s World Championships and will compete in the 100m and the 4x100m relay at the Commonwealth Games in Scotland over the next fortnight

Hunt oozes self-confidence. She is as comfortable discussing Italian opera as Charli xcx. Her apartment overlooks a basilica and one of her goals is to learn enough Italian to be able to read Giovanni Boccaccio’s 14th-century poetry in its native tongue.

‘I live the coolest life,' she says. 'One thing I really love about myself is I go out of my way to create my dream life. I moved to Italy at 21 and live in a gorgeous renaissance city surrounded by artwork. The world’s first botanical garden is 200 metres from my house.

‘It’s a place where I can really enjoy being Amy and where I can build my life outside of track. It’s also so good for training because it’s just us in our little bubble. We go to this track in the mountains which has church towers and the bells start ringing. You just think, “Wow”. If I’m having a bad day, I just go and buy a gelato, walk around and read my book. I really love it.

‘I’m now in a place where I can wake up and say to myself, “I am one of the fastest women in the world”. That’s really cool, it’s something I’ve always dreamed of doing. I’ve been gaining confidence week on week for the last two years. I have to stand on that start-line thinking, “I’m the fastest person here, I’m going to win this race”. Otherwise, why would I be standing on that start line? It’s all a game of confidence.

‘I’ve realised the better way to approach things is with that somewhat reckless optimism. My coach (Marco Airale) prepares us for everything and has his massive spreadsheets with figures crawling everywhere, but once I step on that start-line there’s absolutely nothing he can do.

'Especially with the 100m, there are no tactics involved, no gameplan… it’s all on me. I have to have a radical confidence.’

Posing for photographs in our Daily Mail studio, Hunt needs no instructions on how to work the camera. She explains her OUAI haircare routine to the photographer and discusses her upcoming nail appointment with one of London’s top manicurists.

‘I’ve fallen more and more in love with racing so now that confidence comes easily,' she says. 'I have a lot of love for (American sprinter) Sha'Carri Richardson on the track because she knows exactly who she is.

'Spending an entire day in tiny stiletto heels isn’t ideal for training. I don’t wear heels as often as most women so my feet aren’t used to it'

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence?'

'She doesn’t care if you or I disagree with her. The best sprinters in the world have such a strong sense of self that they’re unshakable. It’s the same with Noah Lyles. I aspire to be like that, too.

‘I love people like Dua Lipa in the same sort of way. She knows exactly who she is and she lives a very cool life. She’s just got married to her gorgeous fiancee, she’s a popstar and she has that sense that life is supposed to be fun.

'You only get one shot at it all, so why would you not live every day with reckless abandonment and reckless confidence? I would like a wedding like hers. I would love to get married in Italy because I have such strong roots there, but I don’t have anyone to get married to right now… so!’

Hunt’s immediate focus is on the finish line at Scotstoun. She became just the fourth British woman to break the 11-second barrier for the 100m last month and successfully defended her British title. Her star is rising and, as a self-confessed material girl, her eyes are only for gold.

‘The Commonwealth Games is overlaid with all these different memories of watching it,' Hunt says. 'There’s a picture of me freshly-born on the changing mat watching Darren Campbell, who is now my mentor. It’s a bit of a full circle moment.

‘Our No 1 priority this year is the Europeans but the Commonwealths will be super exciting because I’ve never done it. People I train with say Birmingham 2022 was one of the most fun champs they’ve ever done, so I’m looking forward to it.

‘I have really big dreams and goals... I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that'

'A gold medal at the Commonwealths would be unbelievably cool. As a sprinter, we always get asked what matters most: times or medals. It’s medals, without any shadow of a doubt.

‘I have really big dreams and goals. When we’re in relay meetings, we know we can challenge the best in the world from this tiny little country. Collectively, we’ve never been stronger.

'I want to win multiple Olympic golds, I want to win world titles and I don’t feel like I should be ashamed to say that. I don’t want to sit here and say, “Now I’ve won a medal, I just want to make the final”.

'I’ve won a silver medal so now I have to back myself towards gold. I have to wake up every morning thinking, “I want to win that Olympic gold”. If I don’t believe in myself, then why should you? I have to be my biggest cheerleader and it excites me. I love the journey I’m on towards that Olympic gold.’

Sports.title: Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next
Sports.content:
Inside Jeff Bezos' bid to buy into Liverpool: The role the Amazon billionaire could play, what 'super smart' £1.35bn investment means for transfer business, how it affects FSG - and what happens next

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

As soon as the news emerged that Jeff Bezos was interested in forming part of a consortium to buy a stake in Liverpool FC, the jokes began.

Anfield was to become the Amazon Arena, a nod to the company where Bezos made his fortune. New signings would arrive on next-day delivery. Liverpool would not just be competing to be champions of Europe but the galaxy, referring to Bezos's part in the 21st-century space race.

Whatever your opinion on the fourth-richest man in the world, it is hard for Reds fans not to dream of the endless possibilities under a man worth £190billion according to Forbes.

But will Liverpool actually see any of the proposed £1.35bn investment? What role, if any, will Bezos play? And is it time for those supporters to get excited?

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to sources on both sides of the Atlantic to help tackle some of the big questions…

Jeff Bezos has discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Liverpool are in a period of transition with Andoni Iraola taking over as head coach in June

What is going on?

Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group are in talks to sell a stake in the club to a consortium backed by Amit Bhatia and funded in part by the family of steel tycoon Lakshmi Mittal.

Bezos is interested in being part of the consortium and other names are also keen to get involved.

Bhatia will be in charge of the bid. He stepped down as co-owner and director of Championship side Queens Park Rangers on Tuesday after nearly two decades at Loftus Road, where he has a stand named after him.

The 46-year-old is the son-in-law of Mittal, the 73rd richest man in the world with £23.4bn to his name per Forbes, and the consortium is keen to buy around £1.3bn in the club.

A spokesperson for Liverpool's owners FSG told Daily Mail Sport earlier this week: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

It is thought that FSG welcome the potential opportunity and this is another way the conglomerate, who also own the baseball behemoth Boston Red Sox, are looking to further position the club for success.

It would be a similar move, though on a larger scale, to when FSG sold 4 per cent to Dynasty Equity in September 2023. Principal chair John W Henry has always been eager for additional investment while still being keen to hold the majority stake.

FSG sources stress that no deal is signed just yet, with the parties in early discussions at this stage, though the fact the consortium has been put together is a significant development. And there are signals that everyone involved is keen for a deal to be done.

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a stake in the Reds

Would it be a wise move for FSG?

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire certainly thinks so.

He tells Daily Mail Sport: 'As far as the potential Liverpool investment is concerned, it looks like it's going to be up to 30 per cent or £1.3bn. That values the club at just over £4bn, which is broadly in line with expectations.

'From FSG's point of view, it's a super smart piece of business. Yes, they have sold part of the club before but this will ensure they still own a controlling stake of around 60 per cent.

'So in terms of the long-term strategy of the club and the individual transfer windows and recruitment issues, it is still FSG's decisions that are being made. If they are selling 30 per cent, that money goes to FSG not Liverpool, so there is no physical impact upon the club's coffers.

'If the club is looking to borrow money at a future date for whatever circumstances and you are owned by Mittal's son-in-law and Bezos, they will be in a position to lend money on an interest-free basis which can only help in terms of cash flow.

'Also, having a potential partner of the magnitude of Bezos does mean there is the opportunity for synergies. If Amazon Prime want to increase their global influence, then one way could be to do a partnership with Liverpool, whether in terms of content or sponsorship.

'Liverpool goes out to the world and Amazon goes out to the world as well. As well out of the world, maybe! He is flying people into space after all.'

Finance experts believe it would be 'a super smart piece of business' from FSG to sell a stake in the club

What is Bezos's involvement?

Bezos, who made his massive wealth by founding Amazon out of his Seattle garage in 1994 and has since launched ventures such as (the unfortunately-named, for Liverpool fans) space company Blue Origin and the Washington Post news group, is interested.

Sky News reported that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia. His exit from QPR on Tuesday, the same day the news broke about his interest to invest in Liverpool, came at a telling time.

The intentions of the consortium are clear, though Bezos has historically been cautious when it comes to major sports deals. He was interested in buying the current Super Bowl winners Seattle Seahawks and fellow NFL team Washington Commanders but pulled out.

There has been an influx in similar deals in recent years, notably Ineos' investment in Manchester United and Todd Boehly with Clearlake at Chelsea.

While Boehly is still seen as the figurehead of that move, Behdad Eghbali and Clearlake run the show. Eghbali loves football and has been pleasantly surprised at the English sporting culture when attending games at Stamford Bridge.

Perhaps we will see Bezos in the posh seats at Anfield before too long, too.

It is believed that Bezos was invited to join the syndicate led by Bhatia

What happens next?

The news of FSG being open to selling a stake came as a surprise to many, including some personnel at the club.

It is not said to be an indication that Liverpool's Boston-based owners, who bought the club in 2010, are looking to sell up. If anything, it is part of their strategic plan to position the club to prosper.

Some fans point the finger at FSG for various shortcomings.

They are no saints, for sure – some of their ticketing policies and price hikes have irked many – but they have done far more good than bad during their time as custodians of the club, including regenerating Anfield and financially backing the club into a successful era on the pitch.

As for the consortium, sources believe they are serious.

The day-to-day running of the club would be unlikely to change if it goes through, but being backed by such mega-rich investors can never be a bad thing.

Sports.title: MLS launches bombshell investigation into David Beckham's Inter Miami for alleged tampering over Casemiro signing
Sports.content:
Former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro’s move to Inter Miami is under investigation by Major League Soccer over allegations of tampering by Sir David Beckham’s club.

Miami announced Casemiro’s signing on Wednesday in a deal to run until the end of next season with the option to extend it until 2029. However, almost immediately MLS revealed that they are looking into an allegation relating to how Miami acquired the discovery rights from LA Galaxy to sign the 34-year-old Brazil international.

The discovery list gives MLS clubs first refusal over prospective signings and prevents them from competing against one another for a player. The Galaxy had the discovery rights to Casemiro but Miami said they acquired them in an agreement believed to be worth around £750,000.

‘Major League Soccer is reviewing a tampering allegation against Inter Miami CF,’ the statement read. ‘The league is gathering all relevant information and will refrain from further comment until the review is complete.

‘While Inter Miami CF and the LA Galaxy have reached a settlement for the discovery priority to sign Casemiro, the terms will be released upon conclusion of the tampering investigation.’

Inter Miami confirmed the signing of former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro

MLS immediately confirmed an investigation has been launched into David Beckham's into an allegation relating to how Miami acquired the discovery rights from LA Galaxy

Miami have fallen foul of MLS’s financial regulations in the past. In 2021, they were fined £1.5m for falsely reporting Blaise Matuidi’s salary, which also resulted in chief operating officer Paul McDonough being suspended for a year and managing owner Jorge Mas being fined £187,000.

The club were also hit with penalties of £1.7m relating to similar breaches involving Andres Reyes, Leandro Gonzalez Pirez, Nicolas Figal and Julian Carranza.

Casemiro is joining Miami as a free agent following four years at Old Trafford after United decided not to extend his contract. The former Real Madrid star helped Brazil reach the quarter-finals of the World Cup earlier this month where they were knocked out by Norway.

Sports.title: Only ONE England player makes FIFA's 2026 World Cup team of the tournament as fans choose Man United star in defence - and cult hero gets the nod
Sports.content:
Only ONE England player makes FIFA's 2026 World Cup team of the tournament as fans choose Man United star in defence - and cult hero gets the nod

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

FIFA have only selected one England player in their World Cup team of the tournament.

After six weeks of action in the United States, Canada, and Mexico, in which Spain ended up adding a second star to their crest after beating Argentina at MetLife Stadium on Sunday, the football governing body has announced their ‘Dream XI’.

The team of the tournament is selected based on votes from the fans, and only Jude Bellingham managed to sneak into the side from the Three Lions squad.

The 23-year-old midfielder netted seven goals, the most-ever by an England player in a single World Cup, as the Three Lions secured their best placing at the tournament since the triumph in 1966 by beating France 6-4 in the third-place play-off.

The majority of the team was completed by the fellow semi-finalists as three spots in the team were filled by Spain players, with three more from France, and two from the former champions Argentina.

Bellingham is joined by Rodri, who lifted the World Cup trophy aloft as Spain captain, and Michael Olise.

Jude Bellingham was the only England player voted to be in the World Cup 'Dream XI'

40-year-old Vozinha was selected in goal after earning cult hero status for his role in Cape Verde's run to the round of 32

The Spanish midfielder was back to his best at this tournament, and his performances in the spine of the champions' side earned him the Golden Ball. Meanwhile, Olise secured the record for the most assists at a single World Cup with seven.

In front of them, the new all-time World Cup record goalscorer Kylian Mbappe, who won the Golden Boot, occupies the right wing, while the man he overtook in his final game of the tournament, Lionel Messi, is on the left.

Messi was the first to break the scoring record, netting five goals in his first two games of the tournament to surpass Miroslav Klose's previous record of 16 goals.

However, the goals dried up after the round of 16 stage, and he has likely finished his World Cup career with an astonishing 20 goals.

In between them is Norway's Erling Haaland, who spearheaded his country to a first-ever quarter-final by scoring seven goals in his first appearance at the competition.

The back four contained Spanish full-backs Marc Cucurella and Pedro Porro, while France's Dayot Upamecano and Argentina's Lisandro Martinez were selected in the heart of defence.

And at the base of the team, in between the sticks, was none other than Cape Verde goalkeeper Vozinha.

The 40-year-old was one of the heroes of his country's remarkable run to the last-32 stage before they were beaten 3-2 by Argentina after extra-time.

As well as keeping a clean sheet against Spain and Saudi Arabia, Vozinha made 18 saves across the tournament and outperformed his xG against by 0.9.

The shot-stopper also hit the headlines for gaining an outrageous amount of Instagram followers throughout the World Cup.

At the start of Cape Verde's World Cup opener with Spain, he only had 50,000 followers on Instagram. But after making a memorable seven saves, that number dramatically increased, with Vozinha now having 29.5million followers.

Sports.title: Jeff Bezos 'holds talks about investing in Liverpool' as Amazon founder - and world's fourth richest man worth $257BILLION - considers joining bid for Premier League giants
Sports.content:
Amazon billionaire Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool.

British-Indian businessman Amit Bhatia is leading a group of financiers which is in talks to make a 'strategic minority investment' in the Premier League giants.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport yesterday, Bhatia, the son-in-law of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal, is pushing for a deal with owners Fenway Sports Group that could take the club's value above £4.5billion ($6bn).

Now, though, Sky News reports that Bezos has been approached to join the consortium and has held discussions about working with Bhatia and the rest of the group. FSG and Bezos have been approached for comment.

FSG took control of Liverpool in 2010 in a £300million deal and have since proven effective owners, giving the club the support they needed to win two Premier League titles and a sixth Champions League.

Liverpool are largely self-sufficient, meaning FSG have not had to invest much - figures published by the Athletic in 2024 indicated that they had only pumped in £136m.

It remains uncertain whether Bezos, 62, will help fund a stake in the Premier League team. Bezos is ranked by Forbes as the fourth richest man in the world. He has a net worth of $256.9bn (£194.9bn).

Jeff Bezos has reportedly discussed the possibility of joining a consortium which is pushing to buy a stake in Liverpool

Businessman Amit Bhatia is part of the consortium in talks to buy a small stake in the Premier League giants

Join the discussion Should mega-rich investors like Bezos be allowed to buy into iconic football clubs like Liverpool?

As reported by Sky News, the Amazon founder has previously considered bidding for the Seattle Seahawks - the reigning Super Bowl champions - and their NFL rivals, the Washington Commanders.

However, on neither occasion did Bezos proceed with a deal.

Bhatia, meanwhile, was co-owner at Championship side Queens Park Rangers. He has a stand named after him at the club's stadium, Loftus Road, but surprisingly stepped down from the QPR ownership setup yesterday.

A spokesman for Fenway Sports Group said in a statement: 'An investment consortium led, managed, and represented by Amit Bhatia has expressed interest in making a strategic minority investment in Liverpool Football Club.'

Nothing is official yet and, if it was to proceed, it would follow a similar structure to a deal made three years ago when FSG sold a small stake to sports investment firm Dynasty.

Bezos founded Amazon in 1994, originally operating it out of his garage. It now has a revenue of $716bn (£534.83bn) - the most of any company in the world - and employs almost 1.6million staff.

FSG has 33 partners including principal owner John W Henry, chairman Tom Werner, president Michael Gordon, as well as NBA legend LeBron James.

They have typically ceded a reasonable amount of influence to managers, being nowhere near as interfering in day-to-day affairs like the owners of Chelsea, Todd Boehly and Clearlake Capital.

Fans have often been frustrated that the club have not taken off the handbrake in the transfer window. The usual policy is for the club to be financially sustainable.

Andoni Iraola manages the Premier League giants, who are currently on tour in the USA

The world's richest people *According to Forbes 1) Elon Musk $794.5B net worth (£593.59bn) 2) Larry Page - $284.5B net worth (£212.57bn) 3) Sergey Brin - $262.4B net worth (£196.05bn) 4) Jeff Bezos - $256.9B net worth (£191.94bn) 5) Michael Dell - $228.4B net worth (£170.65bn)

Last summer, they sanctioned the biggest transfer window spend by a Premier League club ever, £446m, though their club revenues had freed up space for that under Profit & Sustainability Rules.

Liverpool are currently in Chicago as they begin their pre-season tour of the USA.

Andoni Iraola's side play Sunderland in Nashville on Saturday, followed by Wrexham in New York and Leeds back in Chicago, before returning home at the start of August.

Reds fans are excited to see defender Jeremy Jacquet, who signed from Rennes for £60m in January, but more incomings are anticipated.

It has been a slow summer at Anfield - the only other arrival is £34.5m World Cup winner Victor Munoz from Osasuna.

Iraola has identified two areas of concern and has issued an indirect appeal to transfer chiefs to kick on with summer plans.

'It is difficult to say a number when the market is open,' said the Basque. 'You have to be always open to new options to improve the squad.

'There are obvious situations where we know we need to sign players. Winger, for example. We definitely need to sign a winger. In other situations, we will have to analyse what the market gives you, what the cost is, how we see the players we have.

'We have some tricky positions where we have injured players that we trust that are not in the ideal situation. It depends on a lot of things.'

Iraola also said Liverpool are 'very thin' in terms of defensive depth, with Conor Bradley out for several months more yet after a long-term knee injury.

Asked about potential exits, Iraola insisted Alisson will remain No 1 after intense interest from Juventus earlier in the window and admitted he also wants to keep World Cup runner-up Alexis Mac Allister.

The Reds manager said: 'Alexis has been one of the best players of the club in the last years.

'He has had a very good World Cup so it is normal that other clubs want our best players. It always happens in the market. I want to keep my good players. I am looking more to sign new players than losing the ones we have.'

Sports.title: Man United close in on snatching two teenage prospects from rivals Man City as part of Sir Jim Ratcliffe's drive to step up investment in youth
Sports.content:
Manchester United are set to continue their investment in young talent by signing teenage midfielders David Eze and Karim Cassim from neighbours Manchester City.

Earlier this week, United agreed a deal worth £4million plus up to another £4m in add-ons with Tottenham for winger Tynan Thompson subject to the player’s registration.

It’s understood they are now close to signing 16-year-olds Eze and Cassim from City as well, with United hopeful of getting both deals over the line.

Eze has captained England Under-16s but is also eligible to represent the Republic of Ireland, having been born in Dublin before moving to Manchester at the age of six. A powerful box-to-box midfielder, he has also played for City’s Under-17s side.

Cassim featured for City’s Under-18s in their successful FA Youth Cup campaign last season, which ended with them beating United in the final, and has also played alongside United’s rising star JJ Gabriel for England Under-17s.

Assuming both players make the move across town, Eze and Cassim will go into United’s age-group teams at Carrington, unlike Thompson who is being integrated straight into the senior squad as part of the club’s emerging talent system.

Manchester United are close to snatching 16-year-old David Eze from neighbours Man City

City youngseter Karim Cassim is also understood to be close to switching to United

United have stepped up their investment in youth since Ineos took over the day-to-day running of the club, with co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe stating his ambition to sign top young players before they become stars and cost huge transfer fees.

‘It’s not that clever is it buying (Kylian) Mbappe?’ said Ratcliffe in 2024, shortly after completing his minority takeover.

‘Anyone could figure that one out, but what is much more challenging is to find the next Mbappe, or the next (Jude) Bellingham, or the next Roy Keane.’

Sports.title: THE ANALYST - Alex Scott: Why Man United and Arsenal are battling for £80m 'diamond' who's refused to sign new Bournemouth deal - how he dominates midfield despite slight frame, the attributes that wowed Mikel Arteta and United's advantage in race
Sports.content:
When it comes to recruitment at the highest level of the game, it is often the intangibles that set players apart. Is he a good trainer? What happens when he is left out? Does he get on well with team-mates? Can he listen and take on board tactical information? How does he manage disappointment? And can he handle pressure? In the case of Bournemouth’s Alex Scott, who has turned down a new contract offer from the club, it’s his intangibles report card, just as much as his passing, dribbling and all-action play on the pitch, that has Manchester United, Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur circling with intent this summer, with the player valued around £80million. ‘He’s an absolute diamond off the pitch. He’s really, really good and he's one that you'd just want around the group,’ Ian Foster, who managed Scott with England Under 19s and Under 20s, tells Daily Mail Sport. ‘He's such a good kid, and I think he's still under the radar for me.’ Brian Tinnion chuckles when those comments are put to him. When he was Bristol City technical director he brought Scott to Ashton Gate from Guernsey FC, who play in the Isthmian League. ‘The best thing about him is his attitude,’ Tinnion explains. ‘His attitude to play, the attitude to training, and he was never one bit of bother from the minute he walked in the building until the minute we sold him to Bournemouth. He was the absolute dream young person to work with.’ Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott is being chased by Arsenal, Manchester United and Tottenham this summer The former Bristol City man is now valued at around £80million The intangibles weren’t always enough, however, and more concrete hurdles almost killed Scott’s career. His lack of height and physicality as a youngster saw Southampton cast him aside. He had a year at Bournemouth, fell out of love with the game and went back home to Guernsey, where he became their youngest ever player. He decided to take one last swing at making it in England, with a trial at Bristol City. This was likely his last chance, and he had to take it. ‘We organised a friendly game for him against a London academy who wanted to play us,’ Tinnion says. ‘So Alex came across for the week and he scored a perfect hat-trick in 35 minutes – left foot, right foot, header. I'm like, “Wow, who's this lad?”. We'd seen and watched him, but watching him close up like this, he was outstanding.’ He rose to the occasion with England, too. It was Scott’s header, coming off the bench in a semi-final against Italy, that kept the Young Lions on their path to winning the Under 19s Euros in 2022. And it was Scott who started alongside Elliot Anderson in last summer’s Under 21s Euros final, helping to throw Germany completely off their game. So, to answer the questions posed earlier: Is he a good trainer? Among the very best. What happens when he is left out? He often changes games at the highest level from the bench. Does he get on well with team-mates? Nobody has a bad word to say about him. Can he listen and take on board tactical information? Managers spoken to for this piece insist he can take on the most detailed of briefs. What about handling disappointment? Well, after joining Bournemouth in 2023 for £25m, a knee injury restricted him to three games, then a year later he tore his meniscus. He broke his jaw on the eve of the Under 21s Euros, and came off injured and in tears in the final. He bounced back in the season just gone to get Bournemouth into Europe. And though he didn’t quite make this summer’s World Cup squad, he was on Thomas Tuchel’s radar enough to join the Florida training camp. And can he handle pressure? Without any hesitation, yes. Scott and Elliot Anderson, who has completed a £116m move to Man City, were a superb pair in England's Under 21s Euros win last year Scott (left) has impressed Thomas Tuchel to the point he was called up to England's pre-World Cup training camp in Florida Now to Scott’s appeal on the pitch. His versatility makes him an attractive target to many of the game’s elite clubs. Having first been deployed as a wing-back by Bristol City, Scott has moved inside, playing as a deeper-lying No 6, a box-to-box No 8, and an attack-minded No 10 just behind a striker. Where Manchester United are targeting a rhythm-setting defensive midfielder to complement Kobbie Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes, Arsenal are seeking ball-carriers to help get them up the pitch quicker in transition. Deceptively strong, Scott showed last season what an impressive driver of the ball he is, with 21 per cent of his carries deemed to be progressive – stats providers define this as taking the ball at least five metres closer to the opposition goal. That was the fourth-highest mark of any defensive midfielder in Europe’s top five leagues last season. Under Andoni Iraola at Bournemouth and Lee Carsley with England Under 21s, Scott has more recently been tasked with a deeper role, working as a rhythm disruptor. He did that to great effect, particularly alongside Anderson, one of his best friends in football, on international duty.

Your browser does not support iframes.

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta, who values players who can play in multiple positions such as Mikel Merino, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Kai Havertz and any number of his centre backs who can also play at full back, got a first-hand example of Scott’s class in April, when Bournemouth came to the Emirates Stadium and played the Gunners off the park in a 2-1 victory, with Scott getting the winner. ‘He has played for us as a No 10, a No 8; today as a No 6 and he has added a lot of defensive work and a lot of duel-winning to the ability he has on the ball,’ Iraola explained after that match. ‘I’m very happy, because he is becoming a very, very complete player.’ For Foster, it is important that Scott continues to rotate through the roles he can play, rather than keeping him stuck in one position. ‘Whether it’s 4-3-3 or 4-2-3-1, I wouldn't pigeonhole Alex really in terms of a number on his back,’ he says. ‘I just think he can affect the game really positively. I think he's got really high levels of game understanding and he just knows what's required. ‘He's an old-fashioned all-around midfield player. If you would have asked what Paul Scholes and Roy Keane were, they were central midfield players and I think Alex is that. He can get up and down, he can hold midfield, he can burst into the box, he can score and create. He's an all-round, really, really good midfield player.’ Scott's ability to dribble through the midfield is of particular interest to Arsenal, who need players that can break down opposition defences Scott's defensive ability is a lot better than his slight frame would make you expect This summer transfer window will be defined by the market for central midfielders. Anderson has sealed a British transfer record £116m move to Manchester City, Spurs spent a combined £185m on Sandro Tonali and Mateus Fernandes, both Enzo Fernandez (Chelsea) and Bruno Guimaraes (Newcastle) would fetch enormous fees if they were allowed to leave. And the stats show Scott has already vaulted himself into the conversation among the Premier League’s best midfielders, able to turn a match on his own. He ranked third behind Anderson (80) and Guimaraes (75) for fouls won from central midfield last season. He made more clearances than Arsenal pair Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi (both 78) and departed Manchester United anchor Casemiro (73) and ranked third for completed dribbles (29) among central midfielders, again behind Anderson (50) and Morgan Gibbs-White (30). ‘He’s very, very brave, in terms of taking the ball under the pressure,’ Foster adds. ‘He's got the ability as a midfield player to just beat you one-v-one, he's very creative.’ Coaches are also quick to point to Scott’s impact in both boxes, in terms of winning headers and duels at set-pieces, as an area of the game supporters often overlook due to his Jack Grealish-like frame and appearance. But Scott’s situation, in Bournemouth’s view at least, is clear. He’s not for sale. With two years left on his deal, and new boss Marco Rose eager to build his whole project around Scott, Bournemouth have no appetite to sell, and maintain they are desperate to tie him down to a new deal that will increase his price tag - despite the midfielder rejecting fresh terms. Scott scores the winner against Arsenal at the Emirates Stadium in April Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’ That is unlikely to deter United, Arsenal or Chelsea. Scott’s step-sister Maya Le Tissier is captain of United’s women’s team. Her role in any pursuit may yet prove crucial. United have already splashed on midfield reinforcements this summer, signing Youri Tielemans from Aston Villa via his £38m release clause alongside adding Andrey Santos in a £50m package from Chelsea. But United remain in the market for a third midfielder and will be encouraged by Scott's decision not to sign a new contract at Bournemouth. That said, United would struggle to make a meaningful offer without a sale. Arsenal, meanwhile, missed out on Morgan Rogers - who is set to join Chelsea in a £117m deal, topping the record Anderson set earlier this month - but are keen on Newcastle's Guimaraes. Crystal Palace, West Ham and Tottenham, the team he grew up supporting, all looked at Scott in January 2023, before passing up and allowing Bournemouth to get him a few months later. Scott is loved by Nigel Pearson, who gave him his debut at Bristol City; loved by Foster, and has a massive fan in Carsley. Iraola is smitten with him, and may yet push him up Liverpool’s shopping list, and Tuchel is becoming increasingly enamoured with the man once dubbed the ‘Guernsey Grealish’. United, Arsenal and Chelsea know those footballing minds can’t all be wrong when it comes to the intangibles. So, let the bidding begin.

Sports.title: Olympic hero Sir Chris Hoy takes on new role following cancer diagnosis
Sports.content:
Olympic hero Sir Chris Hoy takes on new role following cancer diagnosis

Sir Chris Hoy will start a new job this week after revealing his devastating diagnosis in 2024

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy has landed a new job as he continues to defy cancer (Image: Alastair Staley, LAT Imagesvia Getty Images)

Even as he navigates a terminal illness, six-time Olympic gold medallist Sir Chris Hoy is stepping into a new broadcasting position with TNT Sports. He will be taking on reporting duties for the Games, which gets underway on Thursday.

‌



The 50-year-old track cycling great, who won an incredible 37 medals during his illustrious career, was diagnosed with prostate cancer in 2023.

‌



Though doctors gave him a prognosis of two to four years after the disease metastasized to his bones, Hoy remains steadfast. By candidly sharing his health journey and eagerly taking on his new media role, the British sports icon continues to prove his absolute determination to not let cancer dictate his life.

‌



Sir Chris Hoy's new job

Sir Chris will have a packed summer after securing a TNT Sports reporting role for the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, where cycling will feature among the events.

TNT Sports has assumed full broadcasting rights for the Commonwealth Games from the BBC, which had previously been the home of the competition.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! All the best sports news and much more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



Commonwealth Games 2026 athletes start arriving in Glasgow from around the world READ MORE :

Scott Young, executive vice president of WBD Sports Europe, TNT Sports' parent company, said via The Sun: "Our company has a great relationship with Sir Chris Hoy. We reached out to him to see if he would like to be a part of what we were doing, and we're delighted we're working together again.

"I can't speak for his emotion, but we're delighted he is part of the team. He was a phenomenal athlete, a great ambassador for the sport and a fantastic bloke."

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy was first diagnosed with cancer in 2023 (Image: PA)

‌



Young revealed that Sir Chris' role will see him cover events well beyond cycling. He added: "He will be everywhere, not just at the cycling. It's one of our reasons for having our studio based up in Glasgow.

"So that people like Chris Hoy can not only be in the studio there and telling the story of the Games, as we lead up to track cycling, but then be in the venue and on the ground and able to help bring that to life. This was his decision. And we fully support any other decision he needs to make [health-wise] during the Games."

The cycling legend has cherished memories of the Games having claimed two gold and two bronze medals at the Manchester Games in 2002 and Melbourne in 2006.

‌



Current health status

Speaking in June, Sir Chris confirmed that he is currently in good form. "I'm doing fine, thanks," he told the Press Association.

He continued: "It's trying to demonstrate, rather than just talking about it, that all these people who are in a similar situation to me - living with stage four cancer - that there's plenty of life left in us, and we're determined to make the most of it, and not have cancer define who you are."

Last year, the Olympic great suffered a serious mountain bike accident, which he described as "the worst crash I've ever had" and left him with a severely broken leg. Speaking to The Times recently, he disclosed that remaining active helps him divert his attention away from his diagnosis, while discussing how his recovery from the injury has been a lengthy process.

‌



"It's served me well in my life to try and challenge myself, so if you're going to do something, make the most of it," he said.

View 3 Images Sir Chris Hoy has provided an update on his health (Image: Jane Barlow/PA Wire)

Recounting the accident in November 2025, which took place in South Wales during a mountain-biking outing with friends, he explained: "My lower leg kind of went with it. Basically, the top of my leg was detached from the bottom half.

‌



"I was, like, what have you done to yourself? You've smashed your leg up, you're never going to be able to walk again properly and you've potentially set yourself back with your treatment.

"I'd look at the reflection and it looks like both legs are going the whole way. Strength comes from the neural link - how efficient your brain is at recruiting as many of the muscle fibres as possible. So that's one of the little tricks we used to do to try and keep that mind-muscle connection.

"It does feel at times like you're in a boat with a few holes and the boat is sinking, and you're trying to bail the water out with a bucket. But you know it would be going down a lot faster if you weren't doing the exercise. I often think, with the work I'm putting in, if I wasn't on these [cancer] meds I'd probably be feeling superhuman right now."

Sports.title: Liverpool's £215m summer transfer war chest rests on sales as World Cup-winner could leave
Sports.content:
Liverpool's £215m summer transfer war chest rests on sales as World Cup-winner could leave

Liverpool could raise over £215m in transfer funds this summer as a number of first-team stars, including one World Cup champion, are linked with moves away from Anfield

View 3 Images Alexis Mac Allister is one of several big names who has been tipped for a Liverpool exit this summer (Image: ESPN)

Liverpool's list of supposed transfer targets is growing more intriguing by the day. However, those heading out the Anfield exit could have just as great an impact as Andoni Iraola prepares to make his Merseyside bow.

‌



The most pressing matter of bringing in a replacement for Mohamed Salah continues to plague the squad as they get pre-season underway in the United States. However, more departures may be required before the Reds can comfortably afford the kinds of deals they're after.

‌



There's a wealth of talent at Liverpool already linked with exits who could generate upwards of £200million this summer. Mirror Football examines which major names could depart in the near future and add some substantial figures ready for reinvestment.

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

By all accounts, this represents the least probable departure of the lot. However, that picture could shift dramatically should Real Madrid get serious in their pursuit of Alexis Mac Allister.

Alex Scott puts his foot down with Man Utd and Arsenal put on red alert for huge transfer READ MORE :

The 2022 World Cup-winner has been consistently linked with a switch to the Spanish capital throughout much of 2026. Speculation is once again gathering pace, though there would still need to be considerable movement on all fronts before an exit appears anything close to likely.

‌



The links surrounding a potential departure remain so flimsy that there is not even a ballpark figure being mooted for the 27-year-old. Transfermarkt places his value at around £60m, though Liverpool would undoubtedly demand significantly more, even with just two years remaining on his current deal.

That contractual uncertainty is the sole factor that could suddenly make a summer transfer a realistic prospect. Should Liverpool harbour doubts over Mac Allister's willingness to extend his terms, they may well choose to cash in now rather than risk losing him on the cheap - or worse still, for nothing - down the line.
