World.title: BAY55: 114 Luxury Apartments Planned for Prague’s Riverfront in Smíchov
World.content:
One of the last undeveloped riverfront plots in central Prague is set to become home to a new luxury residential project.

Developer Daramis has unveiled plans for BAY55, a development featuring 114 high-end apartments on Hořejší nábřeží in Smíchov, just steps from the railway bridge and within walking distance of the city center.

According to Daramis, BAY55 is designed to compete with premium residential developments in leading European and North American cities. The company says the project will emphasize architecture, technology, privacy and resident services alongside its prime location.

The residence will include a wellness and fitness center covering roughly 600 square meters, a private residents’ lounge and hospitality facilities.

A restaurant or café is also planned on the ground floor, serving both residents and visitors. The developer says the level of amenities is intended to match those found in luxury hotels.

Designers have also focused on balancing density with comfort. Every apartment is planned to include either a spacious balcony or terrace, complemented by integrated shading systems intended to provide greater privacy despite the urban setting.

Before construction of the residential complex can begin, significant work will be carried out along the riverfront.

The existing Smíchov embankment will be extended, creating additional public space and improving pedestrian access along the Vltava. The infrastructure upgrades are expected to become part of the wider transformation of one of Prague’s fastest-growing neighborhoods.

Daramis acquired the land from BPD Development in 2024. Although the developer has not disclosed the value of the investment, it says BAY55 represents the largest and most expensive project in the company’s history.

Costs are driven not only by the location and construction standards, but also by flood protection measures, advanced building technologies and architectural features planned for the shared spaces.

The project is currently progressing through the permitting process. If approvals proceed as expected, construction of the new embankment will begin first, followed by the residential development itself.

Completion is currently scheduled for around 2030.

World.title: From Müller to Krispy Kreme, Global Chains Are Coming to Czechia
World.content:
International drugstores, fashion retailers, discount chains and restaurant concepts are preparing to open their first locations in Czechia, adding new competition for established players.

Here are some of the biggest brands expected to enter the Czech market.

Müller

German retailer Müller is preparing to launch in the Czech Republic. The company has already established a Czech branch and website, although it has not yet announced the opening date of its first store.

Unlike traditional drugstores, Müller combines cosmetics and personal care products with toys, stationery, household goods, pet supplies and organic food.

The chain operates nearly 1,000 stores across nine European countries and will compete with established Czech market leaders such as dm, Rossmann and Teta.

Krispy Kreme

American doughnut chain Krispy Kreme is reportedly searching for a location in central Prague and could open its first Czech store soon.

Founded in North Carolina in 1937, the company became famous worldwide for its Original Glazed doughnuts and stores where customers can watch the production process.

Ochnik

Polish fashion brand Ochnik plans an ambitious expansion in the Czech Republic, with 15 to 20 stores expected by the end of 2026.

The company specializes in leather jackets, footwear, luggage and accessories. It previously considered acquiring Czech brand Kara but decided to build its own network instead.

OVS

Italian fashion retailer OVS is also preparing its Czech debut.

The company focuses on affordable clothing for the whole family and is particularly strong in children’s fashion. It is positioned between discount retailers and mainstream brands such as H&M, C&A and Reserved.

Normal

Danish discount chain Normal is preparing to enter the Czech market after establishing a local company.

The retailer sells cosmetics, household products, snacks and everyday goods at permanently low prices. Its stores are designed to encourage impulse shopping, with customers walking through a changing selection of products.

MR. D.I.Y.

Malaysian discount retailer MR. D.I.Y. has some of the biggest expansion plans among new arrivals.

The company plans to open around 20 stores in Prague and eventually grow to more than 100 locations across the Czech Republic. Its first Czech store is expected to open at Forum Nová Karolina in Ostrava.

MR. D.I.Y. sells household equipment, DIY products, electronics and stationery.

Burgermeister

Berlin burger chain Burgermeister will enter the Czech Republic as part of its European expansion.

The brand started in 2006 inside a converted toilet building near Berlin’s Schlesisches Tor station before growing into a chain with more than 30 restaurants.

It focuses on its own production, including burgers made with Irish beef and ingredients prepared in Berlin.

Dave’s Hot Chicken

American fast-food chain Dave’s Hot Chicken is preparing to compete with KFC and Popeyes in the Czech market.

The brand specializes in Nashville-style spicy fried chicken, offering chicken tenders and sandwiches with different levels of heat.

Founded in Los Angeles in 2017, the chain has expanded to more than 400 locations worldwide.

Arthur Gelato

Slovak premium ice cream brand Arthur Gelato has already opened its first Prague location on Francouzská Street.

The company focuses on handmade ice cream, fresh ingredients and unusual flavors. It plans further expansion through franchising.

Sticks’n’Sushi

Danish restaurant group Sticks’n’Sushi will open its first Prague location this autumn.

The concept combines Japanese sushi with grilled skewers and will operate a three-story restaurant on Jungmann Square with around 160 seats.

World.title: Five Things to Know Before Flying From Prague Airport This Summer
World.content:
Passengers departing from Prague Airport this summer are being advised to plan ahead as the airport prepares for its busiest travel season in years.

To help travelers avoid unnecessary delays, the airport has released a list of practical recommendations covering transport, security screening, travel documents and baggage rules.

Leave Extra Time to Reach the Airport

The biggest challenge this summer is expected to be road access to the terminals. Construction at the Aviatická–Lipská intersection may cause traffic congestion on routes leading to the airport.

Airport officials recommend using public transport whenever possible, as buses are not affected by the roadworks. Travelers arriving by car should allow extra time to reach the terminals, particularly during peak holiday periods.

Self-Service Check-In Can Save Time

Passengers can speed up the departure process by using the airport’s self-service facilities. Prague Airport now offers 31 check-in kiosks and 32 self-service baggage drop counters, available for flights operated by 18 participating airlines.

Before heading to the airport, travelers should also verify the entry requirements for their destination. Those flying to the United Kingdom, for example, now need an Electronic Travel Authorization (ETA) before departure.

Bring Physical Travel Documents

Although many travelers rely on digital wallets and electronic documents, Prague Airport reminds passengers that electronic IDs and passports cannot be used during passport control.

Travelers should carry a valid physical passport or national identity card, depending on the requirements of their destination.

Security Rules Depend on the Terminal

Passengers departing from Terminal 2 will notice a faster security process thanks to newly installed CT scanners.

The new technology allows travelers to leave electronics and liquids inside their cabin baggage during screening. In addition to the standard one-liter transparent bag containing containers of up to 100 milliliters each, passengers may also carry one extra liquid container with a capacity of up to two liters.

These updated rules currently apply only in Terminal 2. Security procedures in Terminal 1 remain unchanged.

Pack Power Banks Correctly

The airport is also reminding travelers about one of the most common packing mistakes.

Power banks, laptops and tablets must always be transported in carry-on baggage, not checked luggage. In addition, lithium batteries must not exceed 100 Wh unless specifically approved by the airline. Ignoring these rules can lead to delays during security checks or, in some cases, passengers being refused boarding.

World.title: Czechia Debates Social Media Ban for Children as France Moves Ahead
World.content:
France is moving toward stricter rules on children’s use of social networks, while a similar debate is gaining attention in the Czech Republic.

Lawmakers, educators and experts are increasingly discussing whether children should face age restrictions on social media and tighter limits on smartphone use in schools.

The issue has grown across Europe amid concerns about excessive screen time, cyberbullying, online safety and children’s exposure to unsuitable content.

France has become one of the first European countries to push forward with legislation that would prevent children under the age of 15 from creating accounts on social media platforms. The French Senate has approved the proposal, which still requires approval from the lower house of parliament before it can become law.

If adopted, the measure would take effect on September 1 and require online platforms to introduce age verification systems. Companies would also have to remove accounts belonging to underage users within four months.

The French proposal also includes restrictions on mobile phone use in secondary schools, reflecting a wider European discussion about the role of smartphones in children’s lives.

Czech Republic considers stricter rules for smartphones in schools

The Czech Republic has so far focused mainly on regulating mobile phone use during school hours rather than banning social media accounts for children.

This week, the Czech government backed a proposal that would introduce a nationwide restriction on the use of mobile phones and other electronic communication devices in schools. The regulation is expected to come into force in September 2027.

Concerns over gaming, online content and cyberbullying

Supporters of stricter rules argue that unrestricted access to smartphones can expose children to risks ranging from harmful online content to addictive behaviour.

Experts have raised concerns about easy access to pornography, excessive gaming and the development of unhealthy digital habits among young users.

Many Czech schools have already introduced their own rules. Some require students to hand in their phones when they arrive, while others collect devices at the beginning of lessons.

Several European countries, including Spain and Denmark, are preparing similar measures aimed at protecting children online.

World.title: Charles Bridge Undergoes Careful Cleaning as Restorers Protect Historic Stonework
World.content:
The Prague Technical Administration of Communications (TSK) has started regular maintenance work on Charles Bridge, with restorers and specialists currently removing algae, moss and unwanted vegetation.

The work is aimed at protecting the bridge’s sandstone elements from long-term damage caused by moisture and biological growth.

According to TSK, the maintenance will continue over the coming weeks and will not affect pedestrian access or tourism on one of Prague’s most visited landmarks.

Specialists are carrying out the work using climbing equipment and a support boat, allowing them to reach areas that are difficult to access from the bridge itself. The method enables detailed cleaning while avoiding any need to close the bridge to visitors.

Experts say removing vegetation is an essential part of preserving Charles Bridge. Plants and microorganisms growing on the stone surface can retain moisture, which gradually weakens the masonry and accelerates natural deterioration.

Restorers use traditional cleaning techniques

The maintenance is being carried out manually using traditional restoration methods. Workers remove algae and other growth with controlled water pressure, silicone brushes and specialised tools.

After cleaning the stone surfaces, restorers inspect and repair the joints between individual blocks. Damaged sections are cleaned to a depth of around two to three centimetres before being refilled with traditional lime mortar designed to match historical construction techniques.

Charles Bridge is among the most valuable architectural landmarks in the Czech Republic. Construction began on July 9, 1357, under the reign of Emperor Charles IV, after the previous Judith Bridge was destroyed by floods.

World.title: Canadian International High School in Prague: Your Pathway to Top Universities Worldwide
World.content:
Earning an internationally recognized high school diploma and preparing for admission to top universities no longer requires moving abroad.

Canadian International High School in Prague (CIHS) offers students in Grades 10-12 a fully English-language education based on the Canadian curriculum.

Located in the heart of Prague, CIHS combines the strengths of Canada’s education system with the quality of life and accessibility of the Czech Republic. Students receive a globally recognized diploma while studying in a familiar European environment, avoiding the higher costs and challenges of relocating overseas.

An International Diploma Recognized Worldwide

Graduates earn the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD), Canada’s official high school credential, recognized in more than 20 countries. The diploma provides access to over 30,000 universities and colleges worldwide, including leading institutions across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, and Europe.

Unlike the Czech education system, which typically spans 13 years, the Canadian program is completed in 12. As a result, students graduate a year earlier, begin university sooner, and gain an additional advantage as they build their academic and professional future.

Learning the Canadian Way

CIHS delivers its academic program in partnership with Toronto Imperial School, ensuring that students follow authentic Canadian educational standards. Courses are taught using modern curricula, teaching methods, and learning resources aligned with those used in Ontario schools.

English is the language of instruction across all subjects. An international faculty, including teachers from Canada, creates an immersive English-speaking environment that helps students strengthen their academic language skills and confidently transition into universities abroad.

To maintain high academic standards, all teachers undergo a rigorous selection process followed by professional training led by Canadian educators and the school’s academic partners.

Outstanding Value

Tuition is, on average, two to three times lower than at many international schools in Prague while offering an extensive range of included benefits.

Tuition covers:

the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD)

an iPad for both academic and personal use

for both academic and personal use a complete school uniform

an annual gym membership

continuous academic guidance and support

and support educational trips to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and Germany

to the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Switzerland, and Germany participation in the Exchange program in the United States.

International Experience Beyond the Classroom

Education at CIHS extends well beyond the classroom. Each semester, students have the opportunity to join educational trips to Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, Switzerland, and other destinations. These experiences include university campus visits, meetings with admissions representatives, and valuable insight into international higher education systems.

Students may also participate in the Exchange USA program, spending one or two semesters at one of 40 partner high schools across the United States. The program offers full immersion in American school life while strengthening English proficiency and developing valuable intercultural experience.

For students planning to continue their education in the U.S., CIHS also offers the opportunity to transfer to an American high school during Grade 12 on an F-1 student visa, complete their final year there, and graduate with a U.S. high school diploma.

A Modern Campus in Central Prague

The school is located in Holešovice, one of Prague’s fastest-growing and most vibrant districts. Its central location makes the campus easily accessible from virtually any part of the city by public transportation, while convenient parking is available for families.

The campus occupies a modern business complex close to parks and the Vltava riverfront, providing an ideal balance between study and recreation. Students also benefit from an on-site cafeteria and access to medical professionals, including general practitioners, dermatologists, immunologists, and allergists. Sports facilities, swimming pools, cafés, and shops are all within walking distance.

Personalized University Preparation

Beginning after Grade 10, students choose one of two academic pathways: Business & Social Science or Engineering, allowing them to focus on subjects aligned with their future university studies.

Throughout the program, experienced teachers and academic advisors provide personalized guidance, helping students develop essential academic skills, explore career options, and build competitive university applications.

Graduate Outcomes

By the time they graduate, CIHS students have gained far more than a high school diploma. They leave with:

the internationally recognized Ontario Secondary School Diploma

strong academic English proficiency

experience studying in an international environment

university admissions guidance

a global network of peers

participation in international educational programs

access to leading universities across Canada, the United States, the United Kingdom, Europe, and beyond.

Canadian International High School in Prague welcomes prospective students and their families to visit the campus, meet the faculty, and learn more about its Canadian curriculum. It’s an opportunity to experience a truly international education and earn a globally recognized diploma – while staying in the heart of Europe.

World.title: Brasil Fest Returns to Brno With Performances and Public Parade
World.content:
You don’t need a plane ticket to experience the rhythms of Brazil—just a train to Brno.

Brno will once again become a hub of Brazilian culture as the city welcomes the return of Brasil Fest Brno, the largest event of its kind in Central Europe.

The three-day festival kicks off on Thursday, with a full schedule of concerts, dance performances, and street parades bringing a tropical flair to Brno’s historic center.

On Saturday, the festival’s main parade will move through the city center, joined by hundreds of dancers and musicians from across Europe and Latin America.

The route starts at Moravské náměstí and ends at Zelný trh. This year, for the first time, the parade will include a five-meter puppet of the Brno dragon, decorated in the Brazilian national colors.

The festival’s programme will open on Thursday, July 30, with a special concert by Hamilton de Holanda Trio at Špilberk Castle’s Summer Cinema.

The Brazilian mandolinist, winner of the 2025 Latin Grammy Award for Best Jazz Album, is one of the leading figures of contemporary Brazilian music.

On Friday, the festival will move to the city centre with free performances at Moravské náměstí and náměstí Svobody. Visitors can look forward to the Ritmo Factory Big Show, an energetic performance combining Brazilian-inspired percussion, dance and capoeira, followed by a concert from Mirla Riomar, a singer from Salvador da Bahia known for blending Afro-Brazilian traditions with a modern sound.

The main highlight of Brasil Fest Brno will arrive on Saturday, August 1, with the traditional carnival parade through the streets of Brno. Hundreds of dancers, drummers, capoeira performers and other artists will fill the route from Moravské náměstí to náměstí Svobody and Zelný trh, creating a colourful spectacle inspired by Brazil’s famous carnival celebrations.

A warm-up programme will begin earlier in the afternoon, followed by the parade at 16:00.

The evening programme at náměstí Svobody will continue with a Brazilian dance show featuring multiple dance groups, followed by performances from artists including Ely Janoville 4tet and Brazilian singer-songwriter MADDU, whose music reflects her northeastern Brazilian roots and combines poetic songwriting with a powerful stage presence.

The festival will conclude on Sunday, August 2, with a Family Day at Lužánky Park, offering workshops, games and creative activities for children. Young visitors will be able to make carnival masks, enjoy face painting, try dancing and join a special children’s carnival parade through the park.

World.title: Experience Czech History: Ride a 19th-Century Steam Train!
World.content:
Looking to swap your car for something more adventurous?

Take a step back in time aboard the narrow-gauge railway that winds through the Osoblaha region in the Bruntál district, near the Czech-Polish border.

This charming line, originally opened in 1898, still runs today, offering passengers a scenic ride through rolling countryside, forests, and quaint villages.

The railway stretches just over 20 kilometers, connecting Třemešná ve Slezsku to Osoblaha, and is the only narrow-gauge track of its kind in Czechia still in regular seasonal use.

From May to November, visitors can hop aboard historic steam or motor locomotives. With windows down and the rhythm of the train echoing across the fields, it’s a peaceful way to experience this remote corner of the Moravian-Silesian Region.

Find more info here

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kolej na Brochowie (@kolejnabrochowieofficial) History

The railway was built with a narrow 760 mm gauge, and its construction began in the spring of 1898. The first official train ran later that same year, on December 14. After World War I, it became part of the newly formed Czechoslovak State Railways (ČSD). During World War II, in 1938, the line was seized by the German Reich Railways, which introduced eight-wheel carriages and specially designed trailers for standard-gauge wagons. Despite heavy damage to the region during the liberation battles of 1945, the track itself remarkably survived. However, the condition of the trains was poor, and restoring operations required significant effort. By the mid-1980s, the railway underwent extensive renovations, bringing both the track and rolling stock up to modern safety standards. Today, it’s a beloved heritage line, not just for tourists, but for railway enthusiasts from across Europe.

World.title: Alarming: Almost 90% of Hungary now affected by moderate or severe drought
World.content:
Hungary is facing an increasingly severe drought, with almost 89% of the country now experiencing at least moderate agricultural drought, according to the latest data published by the national meteorological service, HungaroMet.

The agency’s latest drought map shows that 89% of Hungary’s territory is currently affected by moderate, severe or extreme agricultural drought. Of that area:

1.5% is experiencing severe drought,

59.4% is classified as heavily affected,

28.4% is under moderate drought.

Only 3.9% of the country remains free from drought, while 6.8% is experiencing only mild drought conditions.

Eastern Hungary hit hardest

The most serious conditions are affecting the Great Hungarian Plain (Alföld), the eastern half of Transdanubia and parts of the Little Hungarian Plain, where large areas are experiencing severe or heavy drought. According to HungaroMet, only south-western Hungary and a few isolated areas in the north-east currently have soil moisture levels considered optimal.

The situation is particularly worrying in the counties that produce most of Hungary’s summer crops. More than 91% of these agricultural areas are suffering from at least moderate drought.

Rainfall has brought little relief

Although scattered showers and thunderstorms occurred on most days during the past week, rainfall was highly uneven. While some localised areas received more than 10 millimetres of rain, over half of Hungary (particularly east of the Danube) received less than 2 millimetres.

The recent rainfall has only moistened the top 10 to 30 centimetres of soil in some places. However, the upper one-metre soil layer remains critically dry across most of the country.

HungaroMet estimates that soil moisture is currently 140 to 170 millimetres below saturation across much of the Great Hungarian Plain and 110 to 150 millimetres below normal in most parts of Transdanubia, excluding the south-west.

Forecast offers mixed outlook

Meteorologists expect wetter air to arrive from the west, bringing showers and thunderstorms through the weekend. Western Hungary is likely to receive the most rainfall, which could ease drought conditions locally.

However, eastern Hungary is expected to receive significantly less precipitation, meaning drought conditions there are likely to worsen further during the coming days.

HungaroMet updates its agricultural drought index daily, providing farmers and the public with information on the extent and intensity of drought across the country throughout the growing season.

World.title: Hungary’s public broadcaster saves nearly HUF 7 billion in first two weeks
World.content:
Hungary’s public broadcaster says its interim leadership has saved almost HUF 7 billion (around EUR 17 million) during its first two weeks in charge, while launching a comprehensive financial and organisational review and preparing a major overhaul of programming.

In a statement released on Wednesday, the Media Service Support and Asset Management Fund (MTVA) said the interim management, which took over on 7 July, had begun examining tens of thousands of pages of contracts and internal documents as part of a broad audit.

According to the statement, the leadership’s priorities include ending political propaganda, rebuilding independent and objective news services, reviewing the organisation’s finances and preparing for structural changes required under Hungary’s recently amended media law.

Contracts under review

MTVA said it has started reviewing high-value production and IT contracts, including agreements involving politically connected companies. The broadcaster said some contracts had raised suspicions that they did not reflect their genuine economic purpose. It added that legal action would be taken if detailed investigations confirm any wrongdoing.

The organisation also announced that it had cancelled programme production contracts worth almost HUF 3 billion for the remainder of the year, describing the affected productions as wasteful or professionally unjustified. According to MTVA, decisions were based on audience figures, value for money, the performance of external production companies and whether programmes could be produced more efficiently in-house.

Football rights extended at lower cost

The interim management also said it had extended the agreement with the Hungarian Football Federation (MLSZ) for broadcasting top-flight NB I football matches for one year.

According to MTVA, the extension was agreed at a cost HUF 4 billion lower than under the previous contract, while leaving long-term strategic decisions to the broadcaster’s future permanent leadership. The broadcaster added that a review of its long-term cycling broadcasting rights is still ongoing.

More archive content and returning programmes

MTVA said nearly 30 hours of Hungarian films and archive programming are now broadcast daily across its television and radio channels.

The M1 television channel is currently operating with a temporary schedule featuring classic Hungarian productions alongside news programming. Meanwhile, Kossuth Radio has restored several traditional features, including the daily noon church bells, and expanded its cultural programming.

The broadcaster also announced plans to bring back almost 100 programmes in its autumn schedule. These will include cultural, educational, religious and minority-interest programmes, as well as returning audience favourites such as Magyarország, szeretlek! (“Hungary, I Love You!”), Család-barát (“Family Friendly”) and Családi kör (“Family Circle”).

If you missed it: Hungary’s M1 television goes off air with on-screen message towards viewers

Audience figures increase

MTVA also reported higher viewing figures during the past two weeks. According to the broadcaster, the combined daily audience share of its television channels increased by 49% compared with the same period last year, while prime-time viewing rose by 61%.

The organisation said the increase was not solely due to M4 Sport’s coverage of the FIFA World Cup, noting that Duna, Duna World/M4 Sport+ and M5 also recorded stronger audience shares. It added that M1 reached an average of more than one million viewers per day during the period.

SUBSCRIBE to our daily newsletter to never miss a bombshell!

Public media restructuring underway

The overhaul follows amendments to Hungary’s media law adopted on 23 June, which provide for the merger of MTVA into Duna Media Service.

The merger will create a new organisation, Magyar Rádió és Televízió Nonprofit Ltd. (Hungarian Radio and Television). Under the legislation, employees working in programme production and supporting roles will transfer automatically to the new entity, while the organisation will have 90 days after the merger to unify its branding and operations.

World.title: PM Péter Magyar: Fidesz support falls below 20% for the first time in 30 years
World.content:
Prime Minister Péter Magyar said on Wednesday that Fidesz has fallen below 20% support for the first time in 30 years, sharing the findings of a new Závecz Research opinion poll on Facebook.

According to the survey cited by the prime minister, the Tisza Party commands 74% support among decided voters, while Fidesz stands at 19%.

“Fidesz has not been below 20% for 30 years, and now it even has a bankruptcy commissioner,” Magyar wrote, referring to the party’s current situation.

He added that the former ruling party was “accelerating down the same slope as the Gyurcsány era”, while his government continued to focus on governing.

“Meanwhile, the Tisza government is working every day for a functioning and humane Hungary. Today, we are deciding on VAT reductions,” the prime minister wrote, concluding: “Step by step. They are left with llamas and spitting.”

Poll suggests dramatic political shift

The latest Závecz Research findings, discussed by pollsters Endre Hann and Tibor Závecz on the programme Szinten túl, point to a major transformation in Hungary’s political landscape.

According to the survey, among decided voters, Tisza enjoys 74% support, compared with 19% for the Fidesz-KDNP alliance.

The research also suggests that Fidesz’s backing among the overall population has fallen from 27% to 16%, representing a decline from approximately 2.1 million supporters to around 1.2 million.

Tisza gaining ground across former Fidesz strongholds

The pollsters argued that Tisza has now overtaken Fidesz in several demographic groups that traditionally formed the conservative party’s core electorate.

According to Tibor Závecz, the opposition has built a significant lead even among lower-income and lower-status voters. The survey also indicates a marked shift among younger voters, with researchers saying Fidesz has struggled to reconnect with a generation it once sought to represent.

Have you read this? ‘Tragic for Fidesz’: Top Hungarian political analyst warns party is wasting its chance to recover

Researchers cite several factors behind Fidesz’s decline

The analysts suggested that one reason for the decline is the collapse of Fidesz’s long-standing image as an unbeatable political force.

They also pointed to the departure or reduced public role of several prominent Fidesz politicians, as well as the impact of corruption allegations and controversies surrounding the use of public funds.

According to the researchers, Fidesz has yet to demonstrate meaningful self-reflection following its election defeat and continues to rely on political messages they believe are no longer resonating with voters.

While they noted that Tisza’s rapid growth could eventually reach a natural limit, they argued that Fidesz’s difficulties show no sign of easing. Endre Hann even suggested that it could not be ruled out that Fidesz, in its current form, may not survive the present political crisis in the long term.

World.title: Hungarian doctor performs mid-air CPR on Ryanair flight as passenger collapses
World.content:
A Hungarian cardiologist has described a dramatic medical emergency aboard a Ryanair flight from Madrid to Budapest, where she spent more than 20 minutes helping to resuscitate a passenger after he lost consciousness, while questioning the airline’s handling of the incident.

According to Telex, cardiologist Júlia Anna Pálfy, who lives and works in Spain, was travelling to Budapest with her three-year-old child on 16 July when cabin crew asked whether any medical professionals were on board.

Asked for medical ID

Pálfy said she identified herself as a doctor but was initially asked to produce a medical identification card. She told Telex that, after explaining she was not carrying her ID, a flight attendant initially said she would therefore be unable to assist. However, as the condition of a male passenger in his forties rapidly deteriorated, she was eventually asked to examine him.

According to the doctor, the man displayed symptoms consistent with a possible heart attack, including severe chest pain radiating to his jaw, breathing difficulties and episodes of near-collapse.

Emergency landing in Marseille

The passenger was moved from his seat and laid in the aisle while Pálfy assessed him. She said she asked the cabin crew what medical equipment was available and was told that only oxygen was on board. She did not specifically ask about a defibrillator at that stage because the patient’s condition had not yet progressed to cardiac arrest.

As the man’s condition worsened, Pálfy advised the crew that an emergency landing would be the safest option. The aircraft’s captain subsequently announced that the flight would divert to Marseille, France.

Passenger loses consciousness

Before the aircraft landed, the passenger reportedly became unconscious and no pulse could be detected. Pálfy immediately began cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), assisted by another, Spanish passenger, while the aircraft continued its descent.

“It was hell,” she told Telex, describing the difficulty of performing chest compressions inside a descending aircraft experiencing turbulence.

Ryanair says defibrillator was available

Pálfy said she did not request a defibrillator during the resuscitation because cabin crew had earlier told her that no medical equipment was available apart from oxygen. She also said the crew never suggested using one while CPR was underway.

In response to questions from Telex, Ryanair said that all of its aircraft are equipped with defibrillators, but stated that the doctor never requested one.

The airline did not respond to further questions asking whether cabin crew should proactively offer the device during such emergencies or whether the crew involved were aware that a defibrillator was available on board.

SUBSCRIBE to our daily newsletter to never miss a bombshell!

Passenger taken to hospital

After landing in Marseille, a French emergency medical team boarded the aircraft and took over treatment. According to Pálfy, communication was complicated because the medical team spoke only French, and another passenger helped interpret.

The patient was transported to hospital in a stable condition. The doctor later learned from the man’s daughter that he lost consciousness several more times in the ambulance before arriving at the hospital. He has since returned to Hungary and is expected to undergo further medical examinations.

Pálfy said that after the emergency, she returned to find her three-year-old child asleep in the arms of another passenger who had cared for the child during the incident.

She told Telex she received a bottle of water and some chocolate from the crew as thanks for her assistance, although she said she would have appreciated a personal acknowledgement from the captain after helping to save the passenger’s life.

The diverted flight remained on the ground in Marseille for around 90 minutes before continuing its journey to Budapest.

World.title: New Danube railway bridge approved in Budapest as Hungary launches EUR 85 million upgrade
World.content:
The Hungarian government has approved the construction of a new railway bridge over the Danube in Budapest, launching a HUF 31 billion (EUR 85 million) project to replace the ageing Gubacsi railway bridge.

The investment is part of the government’s recently announced Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan and is intended to remove one of the country’s most significant bottlenecks for freight transport. Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy announced the decision on Facebook following Wednesday’s cabinet meeting.

Bridge has been limited to walking speed for more than a decade

According to Vitézy, trains have been restricted to just 5 km/h when crossing the Gubacsi railway bridge since 2014 because of its deteriorating condition.

The minister noted that despite the severe speed restriction, the bridge remains one of Hungary’s most important freight rail links, carrying an estimated 10–15% of the country’s total rail freight traffic.

Several months ago, fellow minister and local MP Vilmos Kátai-Németh even filmed himself outrunning a freight train crossing the bridge to highlight the scale of the problem.

“Today we can finally talk about the solution,” Vitézy wrote.

New bridge to eliminate major rail bottleneck

Construction of the new railway bridge is scheduled to begin at the end of 2026, with completion expected by the end of 2029.

Once finished, the project is expected to:

remove one of Hungary’s most important railway bottlenecks;

improve access to the Freeport of Csepel and nearby container terminals;

enable more freight to shift from road to rail; and

reduce heavy road traffic in the surrounding area.

The government also plans to begin preparing the modernisation of the road section of the Gubacsi bridge, along with improvements to the nearby Corvin junction.

Government considering future road bridge upgrade

Vitézy said the railway bridge already has completed construction plans and a valid building permit, but the project had previously been halted under the former government.

He added that the government will also examine whether the existing railway bridge structure could be converted and refurbished for heavy road traffic once rail services move onto the new bridge. If that proves technically impossible, a completely new road bridge may also be required in the future.

Part of a larger railway revival

The minister described the Gubacsi bridge project as more than simply replacing ageing infrastructure. According to Vitézy, it symbolises an entire shift in transport policy after what he described as years of neglect, marking the beginning of a new period of long-term railway investment across Hungary.

The bridge replacement is one of the first major infrastructure projects announced under the government’s 10-year, HUF 3,550 billion railway modernisation programme, which also includes new rolling stock, station renovations, suburban rail improvements and preparations for an airport rail link.

World.title: Sziget Festival 2026 wristband holders offered discounts across Budapest!
World.content:
Sziget Festival 2026 is expanding beyond Budapest’s Óbuda Island with the launch of Sziget City, a new initiative connecting festivalgoers with some of the Hungarian capital’s best-known cultural venues, clubs and community spaces. Wristband holders will also receive exclusive discounts at participating locations between 7 and 16 August.

The project is intended to build a closer, year-round relationship between the Sziget community and Budapest’s cultural scene. Rather than treating the capital merely as the backdrop to one of Europe’s largest festivals, Sziget City aims to present the city itself as an essential part of the visitor experience.

An interactive map available through the official Sziget mobile application will help users locate participating venues and browse their programmes, recommendations and special offers. The festival’s official website describes the initiative as a way for visitors to explore both popular locations and lesser-known Budapest destinations while navigating the city “like a local”.

Sziget City connects the festival with Budapest nightlife

Several dozen venues had already joined Sziget City by the time of its launch. The initial partners include Szimpla, Dugattyús, Arzenál, Turbina, Heavy, Atno, Palazzo Permanens, Pontoon, Szatyor and Trafó.

The list represents several different sides of Budapest’s cultural life. Szimpla is one of the city’s best-known ruin bars, a type of nightlife venue that emerged in previously abandoned buildings and courtyards in the historic Jewish Quarter.

Trafó is an important centre for contemporary theatre, dance and visual arts, while venues such as Turbina and Arzenál are associated with Budapest’s club and electronic music scene.

“Sziget and Budapest are inseparable,” said Ábel Zsendovits, head of Szimpla. According to Zsendovits, the festival and the capital have grown together over more than three decades, helping place Hungary on the international festival and nightlife map.

Márk Drahovszky, head of Palazzo Permanens, said the programme creates common ground for valuable cultural venues in Budapest. He described Sziget City as a community-building initiative based on the recognition that the participating organisations support and depend on one another.

During the Sziget Festival 2026 period, visitors will be able to present their festival wristbands at participating venues to access discounts created specifically for the Sziget community. The offers will be available from 7 to 16 August, covering the days immediately before, during and after the main festival.

Major international performers coming to Sziget Festival 2026

The main five-day edition of Sziget Festival 2026 will take place on Óbuda Island from 11 to 15 August. The official programme includes internationally recognised artists such as Florence + The Machine, Twenty One Pilots, Lewis Capaldi, Bring Me The Horizon and Zara Larsson.

Other announced performers include Ashnikko, Biffy Clyro, Parcels, Underworld, Wolf Alice, Richie Hawtin, Dom Dolla, Sara Landry and Hungarian rapper Beton.Hofi. Organisers say the complete festival will feature more than 600 music, theatre, circus, dance, workshop and sporting programmes.

A special Day Zero will also be held on 10 August, reviving a feature familiar from earlier editions of Sziget. Faithless, Morcheeba and Goran Bregović and his Wedding and Funeral Orchestra will return to evoke some of the festival’s most memorable previous decades.

Festival returns to Hungarian ownership

The introduction of Sziget City comes as the festival begins a new chapter under Hungarian ownership.

Sziget was first organised in 1993 as Diáksziget, or Student Island, before developing into a major international music and cultural event. In 2017, a 70% stake was acquired by the Providence-backed international festival group Superstruct Entertainment.

In November 2025, the festival left Superstruct and returned to the hands of its founder, Károly Gerendai, and the existing management team. Gerendai rejoined Sziget after an eight-year absence, while chief executive Tamás Kádár remained in his position.

The new owners have placed renewed emphasis on Sziget’s relationship with Budapest, its cultural diversity and its identity as an independent festival. Sziget City is one of the clearest signs of that strategy: an attempt to ensure that international visitors discover not only the stages of the Island of Freedom, but also the neighbourhoods, clubs and cultural communities that shape Budapest throughout the year.

World.title: Budapest’s busiest M3 metro to be extended after EU funding secured!
World.content:
Budapest’s busiest metro line is set to be extended after the Hungarian government confirmed funding for the long-awaited northern expansion of the M3 metro.

The announcement was made on Wednesday by Transport and Investment Minister Dávid Vitézy during the presentation of the government’s new Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan. The project will be financed through European Union funds.

The extension will take the M3 metro line beyond its current northern terminus at Újpest-központ to Rákospalota-Újpest railway station, creating a new interchange with suburban rail services.

Mayor welcomes ‘historic day’

Reacting to the announcement on Facebook, Budapest Mayor Gergely Karácsony described the decision as a “historic day” for public transport in Hungary. He said the capital had long argued that no seven-year EU budget cycle should pass without a major metro investment in Budapest.

Karácsony also criticised the previous Orbán government, saying its policies had cost the country valuable time and funding, but added that the new government had managed to “save what can still be saved” by securing EU financing for transport projects.

Plans already prepared for further extension

According to the mayor, detailed plans have already been completed for extending the M3 metro line all the way to Káposztásmegyer, one of Budapest’s largest residential districts. However, he said that, given current financial and time constraints, only the first phase as far as Rákospalota-Újpest can be delivered for now.

Karácsony nevertheless described the project as a major step forward because it can be coordinated with planned suburban railway developments, improving connections for both Budapest residents and commuters travelling into the capital from surrounding towns.

Part of wider rail modernisation programme

The metro extension forms part of the government’s newly announced 10-year railway investment programme, worth approximately HUF 3,550 billion (EUR 9.7 billion). Read more about it here!

Alongside the M3 metro line extension, the Baross Gábor Railway Development Plan includes new InterCity trains, a replacement fleet for Budapest’s HÉV suburban railway, station modernisation projects, preparations for an airport rail link and upgrades to major railway corridors across Hungary.

The government says the programme is intended to modernise Hungary’s rail network and strengthen cooperation between national and Budapest transport developments.

World.title: Orbán declares “We’re fine” as Fidesz launches ‘resistance’ campaign against Hungary’s new government
World.content:
Former Prime Minister Viktor Orbán insisted that “we’re fine” as Fidesz sought to regroup after its heavy election defeat, unveiling a new strategy that frames the party as the leader of a nationwide “resistance” against what it calls Hungary’s new “authoritarian” political system.

Speaking outside Fidesz headquarters alongside the party’s newly elected parliamentary group leader János Bóka, Orbán accused the new government of dismantling the rule of law through constitutional amendments and pledged that Fidesz would fight back using “every peaceful means” available.

Fidesz forced outside after server seizure

The press conference was held outside the party’s headquarters after prosecutors reportedly seized Fidesz’s servers as part of the ongoing investigation into the National Cultural Fund (NKA) case. Orbán claimed the seizure left the party without internet access and unable to operate its internal systems.

“We did not expect to be holding this press conference under these circumstances,” he said.

He described the investigation as politically motivated, arguing that authorities had effectively paralysed the party by confiscating its communications infrastructure and membership database.

Orbán: Hungary is no longer a democracy

The former prime minister said Hungary had entered a fundamentally new political era following the latest constitutional amendment, comparing the situation to the final years of Hungary’s communist Kádár era. According to Orbán, the amendment unlawfully restricted who can stand in parliamentary elections, depriving voters of their democratic choice.

He also argued that the removal of former President Tamás Sulyok marked the collapse of constitutional checks and balances. Orbán claimed the current political system is “illegitimate” and declared that Sulyok was “the last legitimate President of the Republic”, quotes 24.hu. He added that Fidesz would not recognise public office holders appointed under the new constitutional framework.

Fidesz launches “resistance” campaign

Orbán said the party’s newly adopted “Declaration of Resistance” commits Fidesz to restoring Hungary’s democratic rule of law. While he declined to explain exactly how the party intends to organise its campaign, saying he would reveal more details during his upcoming speech at Tusványos, he stressed that all action would remain peaceful.

According to Orbán, Fidesz will continue participating in parliamentary work rather than boycotting the legislature. He also said the party does not intend to dictate the pace of opposition activity, describing Fidesz instead as a “service centre” supporting all Hungarians who oppose what he called political authoritarianism.

“We’re fine”

One of the most striking moments came when Orbán was asked whether Fidesz had been weakened following last week’s political setbacks and poor polling. His response quickly became the headline of the press conference.

“We did not support the creation of this system. We’re fine.”

Orbán argued that the real question is how long former Tisza Party voters will tolerate what he described as an increasingly authoritarian government. He predicted that resistance would gradually become a broad national movement rather than one based on party politics or ideology.

Stay up-to-date: Fidesz’s parliamentary group elected new leader after previous one stepping down

Szijjártó’s new job praised

Orbán also defended former Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó, who recently left Parliament to take up a senior position at Chinese electric vehicle manufacturer BYD. He said he had fully supported Szijjártó’s decision.

“A very important role still awaits him in Hungarian public life. That won’t be tomorrow, but the day after tomorrow. It is also important that he is working in a place that holds enormous value and opportunities for Hungary.”

Bóka added that outstanding personnel issues within the parliamentary group would be settled before Parliament’s autumn session begins.

More on Orbán and Fidesz: Former prime minister says from now on, their mission is “to restore the democratic rule of law”

Private US trip

Responding to questions about his recent visit to the United States during the FIFA World Cup, Orbán insisted he had travelled privately and paid for the trip himself. He confirmed that he had held unofficial, non-public meetings while in the US but declined to reveal any details.

Joking about the cost of attending the tournament, Orbán remarked that he was glad the World Cup only takes place every four years because he could not afford it annually.

World.title: GapMinder, Fil Rouge Capital invest in Croatian healthtech startup Lasken AI
World.content:
GapMinder, the VC investing in technology startups from Romania and Eastern Europe, announced it was leading a seed funding round in Croatian healthtech startup Lasken AI, alongside Fil Rouge Capital.

The funding will support the expansion of Lasken AI’s proprietary healthcare data platform, further product development, and commercial growth across Europe. It follows a pre-seed round from Fil Rouge Capital.

Lasken AI, founded by Patric Jarchow and Leonard Unger, is building a healthcare data intelligence platform that transforms publicly available healthcare information into continuously updated, structured datasets for pharmaceutical companies and healthcare organizations. Lasken AI’s customers include pharmaceutical and healthcare companies, healthtech firms, contract sales organizations, consultancies, and other service providers that rely on accurate, up-to-date market intelligence.

The company’s initial commercial focus will be on the German healthcare market, with plans to expand into Europe’s five largest pharmaceutical markets. In the long term, Lasken AI aims to make its Healthcare Data Foundation available across the continent.

“What stood out to us was the team’s deep healthcare expertise combined with a strong technology vision: creating a continuously evolving data foundation rather than another static database. We are excited to support their expansion across Europe and their ambition to become a key intelligence layer for the healthcare ecosystem, and we are thrilled to co-invest with Fil Rouge Capital,” Cosmin Ochișor, Partner at GapMinder, said.

GapMinder Ventures invests in technology startups created in Romania and Eastern Europe, particularly in Croatia, Slovenia, Serbia, Bulgaria, and Moldova, that are in the seed or late seed phase and are rapidly expanding internationally. It manages two funds. With the first fund having a total capitalization of EUR 50 million, GapMinder has invested in companies such as Druid.AI, FintechOS, Veridion, Deepstash, Siena.Cx, TypingDNA, Medicai, Cyscale, SmartDreamers, Machinations, Frisbo, and Innoship.io. GapMinder Fund II was launched in 2024 with a target capital of EUR 80 million.

Fil Rouge Capital (FRC) is a venture capital firm based in Zagreb, with over EUR 100 million in Assets Under Management (AUM) and a track record of investing in more than 170 startups. The firm remains sector-agnostic, targeting high-growth areas like AI, SaaS, and Fintech with investments ranging from EUR 100,000 for early-stage prototypes to EUR 4 million for scaling companies. In Romania, it recently invested in European social media platform eYou, launched from Bucharest.

World.title: Commercial real estate lending rises 15% in Romania, report says
World.content:
Romania's commercial real estate sector accounted for 54% of all loans granted to non-financial companies at the end of the first quarter of 2026, according to an analysis by real estate consultancy Cushman & Wakefield Echinox based on National Bank (BNR) data. Lending to the sector increased by 15% year-on-year, reaching RON 116 billion.

According to the analysis, commercial real estate remains one of the largest recipients of corporate bank financing in Romania, with banks continuing to support both new developments and the refinancing of existing assets.

One of the largest transactions on the local real estate market was the EUR 400 million development loan granted to IULIUS and Atterbury Europe for the RIVUS Cluj-Napoca mixed-use project.

Other notable examples are the EUR 372 million refinancing secured by AFI Europe for its portfolio of commercial assets, the EUR 305.6 million financing granted to IULIUS for the Palas Iasi mixed-use project, and the EUR 190 million sustainability-linked facility obtained by NEPI Rockcastle from a consortium of local banks.

Vlad Săftoiu, Head of Research at Cushman & Wakefield Echinox, said: “The financing levels granted to the commercial real estate market confirm this sector’s transformation into a mature component of the Romanian economy. The steady increase of the loans’ stock and the continued interest of banks towards financing real estate projects reflect both the quality of the existing assets and the sustained confidence in the market’s long-term development potential.”

“This is not simply a statistical increase in banking exposure, but evidence of a sector capable of attracting individual financing deals of EUR 200 - 400 million, comparable with those seen in significantly more mature real estate markets.”

The report also found that the non-performing loan (NPL) ratio for commercial real estate financing stood at 6.2% in March 2026, up 1.1 percentage points from a year earlier.

While higher than the average NPL ratio of 5.6% recorded for non-financial companies overall, the figure remained below the levels reported for loans granted to companies with state guarantees (11.3%) and to micro-enterprises (7.2%) and small businesses (7.1%), according to BNR data cited in the report.

The findings suggest that, despite a challenging economic environment, commercial real estate financing continues to represent a significant share of corporate lending while maintaining a relatively moderate level of credit risk.

World.title: Abu Dhabi-based proptech company eVoost AI enters Romanian market
World.content:
Abu Dhabi-based artificial intelligence company eVoost AI has expanded into Romania, marking its sixth international market. The company has partnered with residential developer Hercesa Romania to deploy its AI platform for residential property sales.

Founded in 2024, eVoost AI develops artificial intelligence software designed for residential real estate sales. It currently supports projects across Spain, Portugal, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Georgia and, now, Romania.

According to the company, the expansion follows several months of preparations, including meetings with local developers, integration with Romanian data sources, and the establishment of a local team.

“The markets that move first on AI in residential sales will set the standard for the rest. Romania has the fundamentals to be one of our strongest markets in Europe,” said Koh Onozawa Martinez, Executive Chairman and co-founder of eVoost AI.

Hercesa Romania is the company's first local partner. The developer has delivered more than 1,200 apartments in Bucharest and currently has more than 600 homes under construction across three residential projects: Stellaris Residencias, Vivenda Prime, and the final phase of Vivenda Residencias.

The AI platform is already used by Hercesa in Spain and Portugal and will now also support the developer's operations in Romania.

eVoost AI operates on a business-to-business model, charging developers an activation fee to onboard projects to the platform, followed by fees linked to sales performance.

The company, which is part of Abu Dhabi's Hub71 technology ecosystem, says it currently manages residential projects with a combined value of more than USD 3.5 billion across its international markets.

World.content:

World.title: Romanian Parliament convened in extraordinary session to advance PNRR legislation
World.content:
Romania's Senate and Chamber of Deputies will meet in an extraordinary session between July 27 and July 31 to adopt legislation required to meet milestones under the National Recovery and Resilience Plan (PNRR) and avoid losing European Union funding.

The agenda will also include measures to address the impact of the recent cyberattack on the National Agency for Cadastre and Real Estate Advertising (ANCPI), including proposals to extend the deadline for applying the reduced VAT rate to certain residential property purchases.

Senate president Mircea Abrudean announced that the Senate's Permanent Bureau had approved the extraordinary session.

"We will debate and vote on the legislative projects necessary to meet the milestones assumed through the PNRR and to ensure that Romania does not lose the European money it has at its disposal," Abrudean said, as reported by Spotmedia.ro.

According to Abrudean, Parliament will also consider two draft laws related to the disruption of ANCPI's operations following the cyberattack, which halted numerous real estate transactions. One proposal would extend, most likely until August 31, the deadline allowing buyers who had already signed preliminary purchase agreements to benefit from the reduced VAT rate.

"I proposed that all political forces align around a single solution, so that the best option is adopted. The solution is to extend it by a reasonable period, most likely until August 31, so that people who signed contracts and made plans based on the legislation in force do not suffer the consequences of an administrative blockage that is not attributable to them," Abrudean said.

Separately, the Social Democratic Party (PSD) has prepared an amendment seeking to postpone the application of the standard 21% VAT rate on eligible housing purchases until October 1, while the Alliance for the Union of Romanians (AUR) has submitted a bill granting additional time for transactions delayed by the ANCPI system outage.

PSD leader Sorin Grindeanu has also called deputies back from the parliamentary recess, announcing three additional legislative priorities alongside the PNRR-related bills.

The extraordinary session will be held in a hybrid format. The Chamber of Deputies is scheduled to hold plenary sittings on July 27 and July 29, with committee meetings taking place throughout the week.

The legislative agenda includes the Urban Planning Code, a PNRR milestone, amendments concerning the teaching career bonus for education staff, revisions to the health reform law, and additional PNRR-related legislation transmitted by the Senate.

World.title: Romanian households have EU's lowest debt burden
World.content:
Romanian households had the lowest debt-to-GDP ratio in the European Union at the end of 2025, with consolidated household debt amounting to 12.3% of GDP, according to Eurostat data cited by B1tv.ro. The indicator, which also includes debt held by non-profit institutions serving households, declined from 12.5% of GDP in 2024 to 12.3% in 2025.

Romania ranked well below the next least-indebted countries in the bloc, with household debt standing at 18.3% of GDP in Hungary and 19.8% in Latvia. The EU average was 49.4% of GDP, meaning Romania's household indebtedness was around one-quarter of the bloc's average.

At the opposite end of the ranking, the Netherlands recorded the highest household debt ratio in the EU at 93.5% of GDP, more than 7.5 times the Romanian level.

The figures also show that Romania's household indebtedness remains significantly below its historical peak of 22.2% of GDP recorded in 2010.

The Eurostat data challenge the perception that households in southern European countries carry the highest debt burdens. Instead, the highest household indebtedness levels are concentrated in the more affluent economies of northern and western Europe, while Romania continues to record the lowest ratio in the EU.

World.title: Romania’s TTS completes EUR 23 mln expansion of Constanta Port grain terminal
World.content:
Transport Trade Services (BVB: TTS) announced in a note to investors that it completed on July 20 the investment project to expand the storage capacity of the Canopus Constanța grain terminal to 180,000 tons.

The investment comprised the construction of 6 storage silos, each with a capacity of 11,000 tons, 5 buffer silos, each with a storage capacity of 825 tons, a new cargo receiving station for river barges, equipment for one of the two new truck unloading stations, the conveying equipment (belt conveyors and bucket elevators) required to handle cargo flows and connect the new facilities to the existing terminal, as well as 3 weighing stations on the vessel loading line.

The new terminal will receive cargo from both barges and trucks through two unloading stations, each with a handling capacity of 400 tons per hour.

Cargo will be loaded onto seagoing vessels using the 2 existing shiploaders, each providing a loading rate of 800 tons per hour.

The investment, amounting to EUR 23 million, excluding VAT, was carried out by Canopus Star Constanța, with approximately 35% of the project financed from the company's own resources and the remainder financed through a bank loan.

Canopus Star Constanța, one of the three port operators of the TTS Group in the Port of Constanța, is a joint venture owned by TTS (Transport Trade Services) S.A. and Cargill Agricultura, specialising in the handling of agricultural commodities.

World.title: Financier-Turned-PM Plans Radical Cure for Moldova’s Ills
World.content:
Moldova’s President, Maia Sandu, rang Vasile Tofan in October last year to try to convince him to leave the private equity company Horizon Capital and become the country’s next prime minister. Tofan declined.

The businessman and economist Alexandru Munteanu took the job instead. When he then resigned on July 3, Sandu offered Tofan the job again. This time, he said yes.

“This time, I gave it a great deal of thought,” Tofan told media outlet Pro TV shortly after parliament approved his government lineup on Tuesday, with backing coming from Sandu’s ruling Action and Solidarity Party, PAS.

“My initial response was immediate: if the governing party believed I could serve my country, I was determined to do so,” he declared.

World.title: Closed Roads Leave Kosovo-Montenegro Mountain Region Cut Off
World.content:
Authorities in Kosovo have blamed the delays to the border demarcation on “technical issues”.

“Once these technical issues are resolved, the Ministry will work to facilitate border traffic,” the government said.

Montenegro’s interior ministry said “there is not a single problem” on its side of the border.

“Over the last decade, several initiatives have been sent to Kosovo authorities through diplomatic channels for the implementation of this Agreement, but there has been no response from their side,” the ministry told BIRN.

“The reasons for the non-implementation of the Agreement lie exclusively on the Kosovo side.”

The consequences, however, are felt on both sides.

Near Velika, a village on the slopes of Cakorr/Cakor mountain near the Lim River, an old military bunker stands as a ruined reminder that this was once a stronghold of the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA.

“The troubled days are behind us, the years lived under the shadow of watchtowers and military outposts are gone, but we need to move freely,” said 56-year-old Vuksan Vuletic, who spends every summer with his family on Cakorr/Cakor mountain. He joined the road protest last month.

“The states must make a decision on this,” Vuletic told BIRN. “It would make a huge difference if this road were reopened for the entire Lim Valley and beyond.”

In Murino, another of the mountain villages, café owner Nedzad Cecunjanin said the city of Peja/Pec in Kosovo was “like a second mother” to people like him.

“We were educated there and relied on it for many of our needs,” he said. “During the war, it was where we found safety. We have many family ties and godparent relationships there. We even have our cemeteries there.”

“But all of that has gradually been disrupted because we have been cut off from Peja/Pec since 1999.”

“We appeal to the governments of Kosovo and Montenegro, as well as the EU and foreign embassies, to help reopen this road as soon as possible,” he said.

Not everyone agrees. Some villagers on the Montenegrin side fear the reopening of the road may lead to Kosovo seeking more land.
